nodes.name: MainComponent.h
nodes.summary: Declares MainComponent, the application shell that owns the shared AudioDeviceManager, look-and-feel, settings/feedback windows, and every open tool plus its docked or floating presentation container. The single header whose implementation is split across the MainComponent*.cpp files in shell/.
nodes.languageNotes: One large JUCE Component declaration deliberately implemented across many translation units, each grouped by responsibility rather than one giant .cpp.

nodes.name: MainComponent
nodes.summary: The application shell component: owns the audio input service, application properties, tool components and their presentation containers, workspace layout/catalog state, and the settings, feedback and microphone-warning windows.

nodes.name: MainComponentLifecycle.cpp
nodes.summary: Construction, destruction and first-launch wiring for MainComponent: settings folder resolution and legacy-file migration, top-button setup, title bar creation, deferred audio initialisation and top-level layout.

nodes.name: migrateLegacySettingsFile
nodes.summary: Moves a settings file left behind by an older application folder layout to its current destination, so upgrading users keep their preferences.

nodes.name: MainComponent
nodes.summary: MainComponent constructor: creates the application properties store, look-and-feel, top buttons and title bar, then loads persisted settings and the saved workspace.

nodes.name: ~MainComponent
nodes.summary: Tears the shell down in a safe order — detaching tool presentations and windows before the audio service and look-and-feel go away.

nodes.name: configureTopButtons
nodes.summary: Configures the File/Settings/Tools/Help/microphone buttons in the title bar and hooks each one to its menu or toggle handler.

nodes.name: initialiseAudioAfterLaunch
nodes.summary: Starts microphone capture after the window is on screen, applying any persisted device state and session mute flag, so audio setup never delays first paint.

nodes.name: WorkspaceStartupSequence.h
nodes.summary: Tiny header-only policy object that fixes the order of the three launch steps — restore workspace, show window, defer services — as pure logic that can be unit tested without JUCE.
nodes.languageNotes: Template callable parameters keep this JUCE-free so the startup ordering can be tested headlessly.

nodes.name: WorkspaceStartupSequence
nodes.summary: Static helper whose run() invokes restoreWorkspace, showWindow and deferServices in exactly that order, encoding the launch ordering contract.

nodes.name: MainComponentAppearance.cpp
nodes.summary: Theme application for the shell: pushes the current palette into the shared LookAndFeel, the title-bar buttons, every open tool and each auxiliary window.

nodes.name: configureLookAndFeelColours
nodes.summary: Maps the active AppPalette onto the JUCE LookAndFeel colour IDs used by buttons, labels, editors, menus and windows.

nodes.name: applyAppearanceToTopButtons
nodes.summary: Recolours the title-bar buttons to match the active theme.

nodes.name: applyAppearanceToOpenWindows
nodes.summary: Propagates the current theme to the settings window, feedback window, microphone warning and every open tool window or dock.

nodes.name: MainComponentAudioState.cpp
nodes.summary: Microphone state handling for the shell: reacts to audio device changes, keeps the microphone button in sync with mute/availability, and shows or dismisses the no-microphone warning.

nodes.name: hasUsableMicrophone
nodes.summary: Reports whether a usable input device is present, honouring the test-control override that simulates a missing microphone.

nodes.name: updateMicrophoneStateControl
nodes.summary: Updates the title-bar microphone button icon, tooltip and enabled state from the current mute and device-availability state.

nodes.name: updateMicrophoneWarning
nodes.summary: Creates, shows or hides the microphone warning banner depending on device availability and whether the user already dismissed it.

nodes.name: MainComponentTestControl.cpp
nodes.summary: Development-only test-control surface: drives the shell into an approved window state, applies a named geometry, and clicks an approved target for the UI automation harness. The whole file compiles away unless PRACTICE_TAKES_ENABLE_TEST_CONTROL is set.
nodes.languageNotes: Entirely wrapped in a #if PRACTICE_TAKES_ENABLE_TEST_CONTROL guard, so the release binary carries none of it.

nodes.name: applyTestControlState
nodes.summary: Resets the shell (closing tools, hiding auxiliary windows) and then rebuilds it into the requested approved state — microphone condition, tool presentation and workspace arrangement — recording the reached state id only on success.

nodes.name: applyTestControlGeometry
nodes.summary: Resizes and repositions the main window to a named geometry so screenshots are captured at reproducible dimensions.

nodes.name: clickTestControlTarget
nodes.summary: Resolves an approved target id to a live component and synthesises a click on it from the message thread.

nodes.name: FeedbackWindow.h
nodes.summary: DocumentWindow wrapper that hosts the FeedbackComponent form, seeded with the calling context tag and closing through the shell's handler.

nodes.name: FeedbackWindow
nodes.summary: MainComponent::FeedbackWindow — a resizable DocumentWindow owning a FeedbackComponent, exposing setContextTag and an onClose callback.

nodes.name: MainComponentFeedback.cpp
nodes.summary: Help menu and feedback flow for the shell: opens the feedback window with a context tag, counts successful tool uses, and offers an unobtrusive feedback invitation once the policy allows it.

nodes.name: showHelpMenu
nodes.summary: Builds and shows the Help menu, including the entries for documentation and for sending feedback.

nodes.name: showFeedback
nodes.summary: Creates the feedback window on demand (or refocuses the existing one) and tags it with the tool or workflow the user came from.

nodes.name: recordSuccessfulToolUse
nodes.summary: Increments the persisted successful-use counter and re-evaluates whether a feedback invitation should be offered.

nodes.name: maybeOfferFeedbackInvitation
nodes.summary: Consults FeedbackInvitationPolicy and, when it approves, shows the one-time invitation prompt that can open the feedback form or disable future invitations.

nodes.name: setFeedbackInvitationsDisabled
nodes.summary: Persists the user's choice to stop receiving feedback invitations.

nodes.name: MainTitleBar.h
nodes.summary: Custom title bar component: hosts the window title, the File/Settings/Tools/Help/microphone buttons and the minimise/fullscreen/close controls, collapsing into a hamburger menu when the window is narrow.
nodes.languageNotes: Header-only JUCE Component; implements window dragging via juce::ComponentDragger and double-click-to-maximise.

nodes.name: MainTitleBar
nodes.summary: The application's custom-drawn title bar, owning its buttons and drag behaviour and exposing setFullscreen plus an onFullscreen callback.

nodes.name: MainTitleBar
nodes.summary: Constructs and wires every title-bar button — menus, microphone toggle and the window controls — to the handlers supplied by the shell.

nodes.name: resized
nodes.summary: Lays out the title bar, collapsing the menu buttons into a single hamburger button once the available width runs out.

nodes.name: showCollapsedMenu
nodes.summary: Shows the combined popup menu that stands in for the individual menu buttons in the collapsed narrow-window layout.

nodes.name: MicrophoneWarning.h
nodes.summary: Banner component shown when no usable microphone is available, offering a jump to audio settings or a dismissal.

nodes.name: MicrophoneWarning
nodes.summary: MainComponent::MicrophoneWarning — themed banner with a title, explanatory message, an open-settings button and a dismiss button.

nodes.name: MicrophoneWarning
nodes.summary: Builds the warning banner's labels and buttons and binds them to the settings and dismiss handlers.

nodes.name: paint
nodes.summary: Draws the banner background, border and accent using the current theme palette.

nodes.name: SettingsWindow.h
nodes.summary: The settings window: a DocumentWindow with panelled content covering appearance, audio device selection, presets, import/export, feedback preferences and the reset actions, each delegating to a handler on the shell.
nodes.languageNotes: A large header-only JUCE component; every action is injected as a std::function handler so the window has no dependency on MainComponent's internals.

nodes.name: SettingsWindow
nodes.summary: MainComponent::SettingsWindow — owns the settings panels and routes appearance, preset, save, import/export, feedback and reset actions to the shell's handlers.

nodes.name: SettingsWindow
nodes.summary: Constructs the settings window, builds its panels around the shared AudioInputService and binds every handler callback supplied by the shell.

nodes.name: applyAppearance
nodes.summary: Recolours the window and its panels for a new theme and appearance mode.

nodes.name: DockedToolPanel.h
nodes.summary: Presentation container for a docked tool: a titled panel with an options button that hosts — but never owns — the live tool component, so a tool can be reparented between docked, floating and tabbed layouts without losing state.
nodes.languageNotes: releaseContent() exists precisely so the panel can give the tool component back without destroying it — presentation containers are non-owning by design.

nodes.name: DockedToolPanel
nodes.summary: MainComponent::DockedToolPanel — non-owning docked host for a tool component, providing the title, options menu, focus reporting and drag-to-undock gesture.

nodes.name: DockedToolPanel
nodes.summary: Builds the panel's title label and options button and attaches the drag, float, feedback, close and focus handlers.

nodes.name: canStartDrag
nodes.summary: Decides whether a mouse gesture over the panel should begin a tool drag, ignoring drags that start on interactive child controls.

nodes.name: ToolDragHandle.h
nodes.summary: Small grip component drawn on a floating tool window that starts a tool drag once the pointer moves past a threshold.

nodes.name: ToolDragHandle
nodes.summary: Draws the drag grip and raises the onDrag callback once a mouse drag exceeds the start threshold.

nodes.name: ToolOptionsButton.h
nodes.summary: Shared per-tool options button used by both docked panels and floating windows, offering dock/float switching, send-feedback and close.

nodes.name: ToolOptionsButton
nodes.summary: Button that opens the per-tool options popup, with the presentation action label and the presentation, feedback and close handlers injected.

nodes.name: showOptions
nodes.summary: Builds and shows the per-tool popup menu and dispatches the chosen entry to the matching handler.

nodes.name: ToolWindow.h
nodes.summary: Presentation container for a floating tool: a DocumentWindow with a drag handle and options button that hosts — but never owns — the live tool component.
nodes.languageNotes: Mirrors DockedToolPanel's non-owning contract; releaseContent() hands the tool component back intact when the presentation changes.

nodes.name: ToolWindow
nodes.summary: MainComponent::ToolWindow — non-owning floating host for a tool component, providing the drag handle, options menu, focus reporting and theme application.

nodes.name: ToolWindow
nodes.summary: Constructs the floating tool window at its preferred size and wires the drag, dock, feedback, close and focus handlers.

nodes.name: canStartDrag
nodes.summary: Decides whether a mouse gesture should begin a tool drag rather than a normal window interaction.

nodes.name: MainComponentWorkspaceDrag.cpp
nodes.summary: Drag-and-drop docking for the workspace: computes drop-zone geometry, resolves the drop target under the pointer, paints the drop overlay, and applies the resulting layout command when a tool is dropped.

nodes.name: dropZoneBounds
nodes.summary: Computes the rectangle for a drop zone (edges, centre, tab strip) inside the workspace area.

nodes.name: beginToolDrag
nodes.summary: Starts a JUCE drag-and-drop operation carrying the tool identity, with a snapshot of the source component as the drag image.

nodes.name: draggedTool
nodes.summary: Decodes the tool identity out of a drag-source description, returning nothing for foreign drags.

nodes.name: dockedToolAt
nodes.summary: Finds which docked tool panel, if any, sits under a point in workspace coordinates.

nodes.name: resolveDropTarget
nodes.summary: Turns a pointer position into a concrete drop target — target tool plus drop zone — used for both the overlay preview and the drop itself.

nodes.name: itemDropped
nodes.summary: Applies the resolved drop: converts the target into a workspace layout command, re-presents the tool docked, and rebuilds the workspace container.

nodes.name: paintOverChildren
nodes.summary: Paints the drop-zone overlay and highlight above the workspace while a tool drag is in progress.

nodes.name: MainComponentWorkspacePresentation.cpp
nodes.summary: Tool presentation lifecycle: opening, focusing and closing tools, and moving each between docked and floating containers by reparenting the live component rather than recreating it.
nodes.languageNotes: constructToolPresentation captures a juce::Component::SafePointer in every handler lambda, so callbacks fired after teardown are no-ops rather than dangling calls.

nodes.name: presentTool
nodes.summary: Presents a tool in the requested presentation, creating its component on first use, detaching any previous container and rebuilding the workspace around it.

nodes.name: constructToolPresentation
nodes.summary: Builds the DockedToolPanel or ToolWindow for a tool, binding SafePointer-guarded drag, dock/float, feedback, close and focus handlers and restoring saved floating bounds.

nodes.name: focusTool
nodes.summary: Brings a tool's container to the front and gives it keyboard focus, recording the focus for workspace state.

nodes.name: closeTool
nodes.summary: Closes a tool: tears down its presentation container, releases the tool component and its audio consumer registration, and updates the workspace layout.

nodes.name: createToolComponent
nodes.summary: Factory that instantiates the tuner, spectrogram or harmonic analyzer component for a tool type.

nodes.name: detachToolPresentation
nodes.summary: Removes a tool from its current docked panel or floating window without destroying the tool component, saving floating bounds on the way out.

nodes.name: applyAppearanceToTool
nodes.summary: Pushes the current theme into a tool component and its presentation container.

nodes.name: MainComponentWorkspaceSnapshot.cpp
nodes.summary: Captures the live workspace into a serialisable snapshot and applies a snapshot back onto the shell, including per-tool settings payloads with bounds-checked decoding.
nodes.languageNotes: Payload numbers are clamped on decode so a hand-edited or corrupted settings file cannot push the tuner into an invalid configuration.

nodes.name: boundedPayloadNumber
nodes.summary: Reads a numeric field from a tool settings payload and clamps it into the accepted range, falling back when the field is missing or non-numeric.

nodes.name: boundedPayloadInteger
nodes.summary: Integer counterpart of boundedPayloadNumber for clamped payload fields.

nodes.name: decodeTunerPayload
nodes.summary: Rebuilds TunerSettings from a stored payload, validating every field against the tuner's accepted ranges.

nodes.name: captureActiveWorkspace
nodes.summary: Snapshots the current layout, floating tool bounds and per-tool settings into a WorkspaceSnapshot for saving or naming.

nodes.name: applyWorkspaceSnapshot
nodes.summary: Applies a workspace snapshot by planning and executing the presentation changes, restoring layout, bounds and per-tool settings.

nodes.name: main.cpp
nodes.summary: JUCE application entry point: declares PracticeTakesApplication and the top-level DocumentWindow, parses the command-line flags (version, mute microphone, UI validation, test control, Performance Lab) and drives the startup sequence.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses raw X11 calls on Linux to set the fullscreen window property, since JUCE's own fullscreen handling does not cover the window-manager hint.

nodes.name: PracticeTakesApplication
nodes.summary: The juce::JUCEApplication subclass that owns the main window for the lifetime of the process and implements startup, shutdown and quit.

nodes.name: setOperatingSystemFullscreen
nodes.summary: Sets or clears the window manager's fullscreen state for a component, using X11 atoms on Linux.

nodes.name: initialise
nodes.summary: Parses the command line — version, --mute-microphone, --ui-validation-scenario, --test-state, --test-control, --automate-performance-lab — rejects flags whose feature was not compiled in, and creates the main window.

nodes.name: FeedbackComponent.cpp
nodes.summary: Implementation of the in-app feedback form: draft persistence, validation, screenshot capture, a preview dialog and the background HTTPS submission to the feedback-intake worker.
nodes.languageNotes: Submission runs on a juce::Thread with an https-only endpoint check; the UI thread never blocks on the network request.

nodes.name: FeedbackPreview
nodes.summary: Small component that renders the assembled feedback text alongside the captured screenshot in the preview dialog.

nodes.name: FeedbackComponent
nodes.summary: Builds the whole feedback form — type selector, title, description, reproduction, email, context and environment diagnostics — and restores any saved draft.

nodes.name: resized
nodes.summary: Lays out the feedback form's labels, editors, diagnostics and action buttons.

nodes.name: currentDraft
nodes.summary: Collects the current editor contents into a draft value object used for validation, preview, persistence and submission.

nodes.name: validate
nodes.summary: Validates the draft — required fields and email shape — and reports the first problem through the validation label.

nodes.name: previewText
nodes.summary: Renders the draft into the exact human-readable payload text that will be submitted, so the user sees what is sent.

nodes.name: captureApplicationScreenshot
nodes.summary: Captures an image of the application window for attachment, excluding the feedback form itself and downscaling it to a bounded size.

nodes.name: preview
nodes.summary: Validates the draft and, if it passes, opens the preview dialog showing the assembled report and screenshot.

nodes.name: submit
nodes.summary: Validates the draft, moves the form into its submitting state and starts the background request thread.

nodes.name: sendRequest
nodes.summary: Posts the feedback JSON to the configured https endpoint and returns the status code and response body.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Background thread body that builds the request payload, sends it, and marshals the success or failure result back to the message thread, clearing the saved draft on success.

nodes.name: FeedbackComponent.h
nodes.summary: Declares FeedbackComponent, the in-app feedback form component with its editors, diagnostics, draft state and background submission request.

nodes.name: FeedbackComponent
nodes.summary: The feedback form component: owns every editor and label, the pending draft, submission state and the locked active request used for background submission.

nodes.name: FeedbackInvitationPolicy.h
nodes.summary: Pure, JUCE-free policy deciding when to offer a feedback invitation: after three successful tool uses, only once, never while a live session is active, and never after the user opts out.
nodes.languageNotes: constexpr and header-only with no JUCE dependency, following the project's split of pure logic out of Component classes so it can be unit tested headlessly.

nodes.name: shouldInvite
nodes.summary: Returns true only when no live session is active, the invitation has not been shown, invitations are not disabled, and the successful-use threshold is met.

nodes.name: ApplicationLaunchTimer.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements the launch timer: records the moment the main window becomes visible and exposes the elapsed launch duration through a process-wide instance.

nodes.name: ApplicationLaunchTimer.h
nodes.summary: Declares ApplicationLaunchTimer, which measures the interval between process start and the main window becoming visible.

nodes.name: ApplicationLaunchTimer
nodes.summary: Holds the process start time and, once markMainWindowVisible is called, the resulting launch duration.

nodes.name: WorkspaceStartupSequenceTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 test asserting that WorkspaceStartupSequence::run invokes restore-workspace, show-window and defer-services in that exact order.

nodes.name: FeedbackInvitationPolicyTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 tests covering FeedbackInvitationPolicy::shouldInvite across the use-count threshold, already-shown, opted-out and live-session cases.

nodes.name: ApplicationLaunchTimerTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 test verifying that ApplicationLaunchTimer reports the elapsed duration between process start and the main window becoming visible.

nodes.name: BenchmarkInterfaces.h
nodes.summary: Declares the abstract seams of the Performance Lab benchmarking framework: the BenchmarkClock, TelemetryCollector, BenchmarkScenario and OptimizationStrategy interfaces plus the StrategyParameter/ValidationResult value types they exchange.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure abstract base classes with virtual destructors and [[nodiscard]] const-noexcept accessors — the dependency-inversion boundary that lets the runner be unit tested without JUCE or real audio.

nodes.name: BenchmarkRecordCodec.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements the bidirectional JSON codec for BenchmarkRunRecord, encoding and decoding configuration, provenance, trials and summaries via juce::var, including schema-version migration and forward-version rejection.
nodes.languageNotes: Free helper functions live in an anonymous namespace; decoding is defensive and returns a RecordDecodeResult rather than throwing.

nodes.name: BenchmarkRecordCodec.h
nodes.summary: Public surface of the benchmark record serializer: the RecordDecodeStatus/RecordDecodeResult result types and the static BenchmarkRecordCodec encode/decode entry points.

nodes.name: BenchmarkRecordStore.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements the on-disk benchmark record store: run-id sanitisation that blocks directory escape, immutable write-once saves, JSON loads with error classification, run-id listing, and standalone record export.
nodes.languageNotes: Run identifiers are rejected if they contain path separators, '..' or a leading '~', keeping every write inside the record directory.

nodes.name: BenchmarkRecordStore.h
nodes.summary: Declares the file-backed BenchmarkRecordStore (save/load/listRunIds) with its RecordStoreStatus outcome enum and StoredRecordResult payload, plus the free exportBenchmarkRecord helper.

nodes.name: BenchmarkTypes.h
nodes.summary: Central value-type vocabulary for the Performance Lab: run configuration, provenance, trial measurements, metric summaries and the composite BenchmarkRunRecord, together with the record schema version and status/warning enums.
nodes.languageNotes: Header-only aggregate structs with in-class default member initialisers; benchmarkRecordSchemaVersion is the single source of truth for record compatibility.

nodes.name: InTreeOptimizationStrategy.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements the callback-driven OptimizationStrategy adapter, storing the injected identity strings, parameter schema and validator/compatibility/activate/deactivate callables and forwarding each virtual call to them.

nodes.name: InTreeOptimizationStrategy.h
nodes.summary: Declares a concrete OptimizationStrategy that is composed from std::function callbacks, so an optimization variant can be defined in-tree without writing a new subclass.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses std::function-typed aliases (Validator, Compatibility, Activator, Deactivator) to turn subclassing into construction-time composition.

nodes.name: NonRealTimeTelemetryCollector.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements message-thread telemetry gathering: samples process CPU/memory and ambient load around each trial, folds recorded GUI latencies and completed-work counts into metric samples, and emits a TrialMeasurement on endTrial.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately non-real-time — all sampling and allocation happens on the message thread, never inside the audio callback.

nodes.name: NonRealTimeTelemetryCollector.h
nodes.summary: Declares the ProcessMetricsSnapshot/ProcessMetricsProvider seam and the NonRealTimeTelemetryCollector that implements TelemetryCollector on top of it plus an injected BenchmarkClock.

nodes.name: PlatformProvenanceProvider.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements JUCE-backed host detection (OS name, CPU model, physical memory, active audio device/backend/sample-rate/buffer-size) and folds it into a RunProvenance, substituting an explicit 'unknown' marker for anything unavailable.
nodes.languageNotes: Every unavailable field becomes the literal 'unknown' rather than an empty string, so comparability checks can flag it instead of silently treating runs as equivalent.

nodes.name: PlatformProvenanceProvider.h
nodes.summary: Declares the PlatformMetadata value type, the injectable PlatformMetadataSource interface, its JUCE implementation, and the PlatformProvenanceProvider that turns detected metadata into RunProvenance.

nodes.name: StrategyRegistry.cpp
nodes.summary: Builds the in-process catalogue of optimization strategies, registering the 'baseline' production strategy and a 'parameterized-fixture' strategy with integer batchSize validation, and creates a fresh instance per lookup.
nodes.languageNotes: Factories are std::function closures, so create() always yields an independent instance rather than sharing registry-owned state.

nodes.name: ValidationResult
nodes.summary: Aggregate carrying a validity flag and human-readable error list, with success()/failure() factory helpers used by scenario and strategy validation.

nodes.name: BenchmarkClock
nodes.summary: Abstract time source returning a steady_clock time point, injected so tests can drive benchmark timing deterministically.

nodes.name: TelemetryCollector
nodes.summary: Abstract per-trial measurement collector with beginTrial/endTrial/abortTrial, decoupling the runner from how metrics are actually sampled.

nodes.name: BenchmarkScenario
nodes.summary: Abstract benchmark workload contract: identity metadata, configuration validation, prepare/runTrial/restore lifecycle and post-run correctness verification.

nodes.name: OptimizationStrategy
nodes.summary: Abstract optimization variant contract exposing identity, a declarative parameter schema, parameter validation, scenario compatibility and activate/deactivate hooks.

nodes.name: RunConfiguration
nodes.summary: Describes what a benchmark run should execute: scenario and workload ids, strategy id and parameters, warm-up and measured trial counts, and the audio configuration.

nodes.name: RunProvenance
nodes.summary: Captures the environment a run was measured in — app version, commit, build type, OS, CPU, memory, audio setup and instrumentation overhead status — so results can be compared honestly.

nodes.name: TrialMeasurement
nodes.summary: One measured trial: index, start timestamp, wall duration, metric samples and counts of deadline misses, dropouts and underruns.

nodes.name: MetricSummary
nodes.summary: Aggregated statistics for a single metric across trials: sample count, median, tail percentile, min, max and variability.

nodes.name: BenchmarkRunRecord
nodes.summary: The complete persisted artifact of a benchmark run: schema version, run id, status, configuration, provenance, trials, summaries and warnings.

nodes.name: BenchmarkRecordCodec
nodes.summary: Stateless codec exposing static encode/decode between BenchmarkRunRecord and juce::var JSON.

nodes.name: encodeProvenance
nodes.summary: Serializes RunProvenance — version, commit, build type, OS, CPU, optional memory, nested audio configuration and instrumentation overhead status — into a JSON object.

nodes.name: decodeProvenance
nodes.summary: Rebuilds RunProvenance from JSON, tolerating absent optional fields and mapping the instrumentation overhead status string back to its enum.

nodes.name: encodeTrial
nodes.summary: Serializes a TrialMeasurement including its start timestamp, nanosecond duration, metric sample array and real-time event counters.

nodes.name: decodeTrial
nodes.summary: Reconstructs a TrialMeasurement from JSON, restoring the timestamp, duration and per-metric samples.

nodes.name: encode
nodes.summary: Top-level encoder producing the full benchmark record JSON object with schema version, status, configuration, provenance, trials, summaries and warnings.

nodes.name: decode
nodes.summary: Top-level decoder that validates the schema version, rejects newer schemas, migrates legacy records and returns a RecordDecodeResult with either the record or an error message.

nodes.name: BenchmarkRecordStore
nodes.summary: Directory-backed store that writes one immutable JSON file per benchmark run and can load or enumerate them by run id.

nodes.name: save
nodes.summary: Validates the run id, creates the record directory, refuses to overwrite an existing run, and writes the codec-encoded JSON.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Reads a stored run by id and maps missing files, unparseable JSON and newer schema versions onto distinct RecordStoreStatus outcomes.

nodes.name: listRunIds
nodes.summary: Enumerates JSON files in the record directory and returns their run identifiers.

nodes.name: exportBenchmarkRecord
nodes.summary: Writes a benchmark record to an arbitrary destination file outside the store, used for sharing or archiving a run.

nodes.name: InTreeOptimizationStrategy
nodes.summary: Concrete OptimizationStrategy built from injected identity strings, a parameter schema and validator/compatibility/activate/deactivate callables.

nodes.name: InTreeOptimizationStrategy
nodes.summary: Constructor moving the identity strings, parameter schema and the four behaviour callbacks into the strategy instance.

nodes.name: ProcessMetricsProvider
nodes.summary: Abstract source of process CPU, process memory and ambient CPU samples, injected so telemetry can be tested without touching the OS.

nodes.name: NonRealTimeTelemetryCollector
nodes.summary: TelemetryCollector implementation that samples process metrics and GUI latency on the message thread and turns each trial into a TrialMeasurement.

nodes.name: beginTrial
nodes.summary: Starts a trial by recording the index and start time from the injected clock and clearing the per-trial GUI latency and completed-work accumulators.

nodes.name: endTrial
nodes.summary: Closes the active trial, samples process/ambient metrics, derives GUI latency and throughput metric samples, and returns the assembled TrialMeasurement.

nodes.name: PlatformMetadataSource
nodes.summary: Abstract host-metadata source returning OS, CPU, memory and audio configuration, injected to keep provenance tests hermetic.

nodes.name: JucePlatformMetadataSource
nodes.summary: JUCE-backed PlatformMetadataSource that reads host details and, optionally, the live AudioDeviceManager's current device settings.

nodes.name: PlatformProvenanceProvider
nodes.summary: Turns detected platform metadata into a RunProvenance record for a benchmark run.

nodes.name: detect
nodes.summary: Collects OS name, CPU model, physical memory and the active audio device name, backend, sample rate and buffer size from JUCE, tolerating a missing audio device.

nodes.name: collect
nodes.summary: Assembles a RunProvenance from the metadata source, substituting the explicit 'unknown' marker wherever a value could not be determined.

nodes.name: StrategyRegistry
nodes.summary: Constructor registering the built-in strategies: 'baseline', which accepts no parameters, and 'parameterized-fixture', which validates a positive integer batchSize.

nodes.name: ids
nodes.summary: Returns the identifiers of every registered strategy in registration order.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Looks up a strategy identifier and invokes its factory, returning a fresh owning instance or nullptr when unknown.

nodes.name: StrategyRegistry.h
nodes.summary: Declares the StrategyRegistry that maps strategy identifiers to factory callables and hands out owning std::unique_ptr<OptimizationStrategy> instances.

nodes.name: TrialAggregator.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements deterministic statistics over completed trials: groups metric samples by id, rejects non-finite values and inconsistent units, and emits median, p95 tail, min, max and population standard deviation per metric alongside summed event totals.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a std::map keyed by metric id so summaries come out in a stable, alphabetically ordered sequence regardless of sample arrival order.

nodes.name: TrialAggregator.h
nodes.summary: Declares the TrialEventTotals/TrialAggregation results and the stateless TrialAggregator that reduces a list of TrialMeasurement values into metric summaries.

nodes.name: BenchmarkInterfacesTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 tests pinning the BenchmarkScenario and OptimizationStrategy contracts, verifying stable metadata accessors and that validation failures return actionable error messages.

nodes.name: BenchmarkRecordCodecTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 tests covering a full encode/decode round trip of a benchmark record, schema-version-one migration of the instrumentation overhead status, and rejection of forward schema versions.

nodes.name: BenchmarkRecordStoreTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 tests for the record store using a temporary directory fixture: immutable one-file-per-run saves, listing and loading, corrupt/newer-schema error propagation, run-id path-escape rejection, and atomic export.

nodes.name: BenchmarkTypesTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 tests asserting the default state of BenchmarkRunRecord (current schema version, pending status) and that configuration, provenance, trials and summaries compose correctly.

nodes.name: InTreeOptimizationStrategyTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 tests exercising a parameterized in-tree strategy against baseline and confirming both variants share a single executable implementation.

nodes.name: NonRealTimeTelemetryCollectorTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 tests driving the telemetry collector with a fake metrics provider and clock, checking process/GUI/ambient/throughput metric emission and that aborting a trial discards trial-local markers.

nodes.name: PlatformProvenanceProviderTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 tests verifying provenance merges build and audio metadata, explicitly marks unavailable values as unknown, and that the JUCE source still detects the host with no audio device present.

nodes.name: StrategyRegistryTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 tests asserting the registry exposes the production baseline and runtime fixture strategies and returns independent instances on each create call.

nodes.name: TrialAggregatorTests.cpp

nodes.name: ToolSettingsPayload

nodes.name: WorkspaceNode
nodes.summary: Recursive dock-tree node that is either a single tool leaf, a tab group or an orientated split with a ratio and two children, with deep-copy semantics and static factories.

nodes.name: FloatingWorkspaceTool
nodes.summary: Describes a tool presented as a floating window, pairing its tool id with persisted bounds.

nodes.name: WorkspaceSnapshot

nodes.name: NamedWorkspace
nodes.summary: A user- or built-in-named workspace: stable id, display name and its snapshot.

nodes.name: WorkspaceCatalog
nodes.summary: Versioned top-level document holding the active snapshot, the id of the source it came from and all named workspaces.

nodes.name: split

nodes.name: presentationOf

nodes.name: contains

nodes.name: WorkspaceNormalizer
nodes.summary: Static normalizer that sanitizes a workspace snapshot against the tool registry, structural limits and available display areas, producing a safe snapshot plus a recovery report.

nodes.name: WorkspaceNormalizationReport
nodes.summary: Flags describing which safety measures fired during normalization: fallback used, depth limit exceeded, collection limit exceeded.

nodes.name: WorkspaceNormalizationResult
nodes.summary: Pairs the normalized snapshot with its normalization report.

nodes.name: normalize
nodes.summary: Normalizes a whole snapshot: rebuilds the dock tree, filters unknown or duplicate tools, caps floating tools and settings entries, constrains bounds and falls back to a default layout when empty.

nodes.name: normalizeNode
nodes.summary: Recursively normalizes a dock node, enforcing the depth limit, tab cap and split-ratio range while dropping unresolvable tool ids.

nodes.name: normalizeLeaf

nodes.name: constrainBounds
nodes.summary: Clamps a rectangle so it stays visible within one of the supplied display areas, recentering it when it lies fully off-screen.

nodes.name: WorkspaceSessionLifecycle
nodes.summary: Static coordinator for workspace session restore, active-snapshot capture and reset, layering normalization and built-in fallbacks over the persisted catalog.

nodes.name: sourceExists

nodes.name: WorkspaceSnapshotApply
nodes.summary: Static planner/executor that converts a workspace snapshot into tool open/close directives and a WorkspaceLayoutState tree, then applies them via injected callbacks.

nodes.name: convertNode

nodes.name: WorkspaceSnapshotApplyTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 tests asserting that planning a snapshot yields the right tool open/close directives and layout tree, and that execute invokes callbacks in order.

nodes.summary: Holds the set of known tool definitions and resolves an arbitrary tool id (including legacy aliases) to a canonical definition.

nodes.summary: Describes one registrable tool: canonical id, accepted aliases and the version of its settings payload.

nodes.name: isDarkTheme
nodes.summary: Constexpr predicate reporting whether the given Theme is the dark variant.

nodes.name: settingsOptions

nodes.summary: RAII fixture that creates a unique temporary settings file and deletes it on destruction.

nodes.summary: Defines the closed vocabulary the manual GUI harness may address: the table of approved window states, the table of clickable objects, the named window geometries, and the tool names those states reference. Lookups return null for unapproved names so a drifted harness fails loudly.

nodes.name: ApprovedWindowStates.h
nodes.summary: Declares the JUCE-free vocabulary types for the test-control channel: ToolPresentation/WorkspaceArrangement enums, the ApprovedWindowState and ApprovedClickTarget structs, and the accessor/lookup API over the approved tables.

nodes.name: TestControlChannel.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements the background reader thread for the test-control channel: reads command lines from stdin, marshals each one onto the JUCE message thread via callAsync and a promise/future handshake, and writes the rendered response back to stdout.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses std::promise/std::future to block the reader thread while the message thread executes the command, keeping all UI mutation on the message thread.

nodes.name: TestControlChannel.h
nodes.summary: Declares the juce::Thread-based TestControlChannel plus FunctionTestControlTarget, a std::function-backed adapter that lets the application shell supply the target behaviour without subclassing.

nodes.name: TestControlClicker.cpp
nodes.summary: Resolves an approved object id to a live juce::Component and invokes its action directly, checking effective visibility up the parent chain and enabled state first. No pointer motion or synthetic input is involved.

nodes.name: TestControlClicker.h
nodes.summary: Declares the component-resolution helpers used by the click command: findComponentById, isEffectivelyVisible, and clickComponentById.
nodes.languageNotes: Includes juce_gui_basics directly instead of JuceHeader.h so it stays within the module set the test binary links.

nodes.name: TestControlCommand.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements strict tokenising and parsing of test-control command lines into a Command struct, rejecting unknown verbs, missing arguments, and trailing extras, plus the inverse verb-name mapping.

nodes.name: TestControlCommand.h

nodes.name: TestControlSession.cpp

nodes.name: TestControlSession.h

nodes.languageNotes: Pure-virtual interface with a virtual destructor; the seam that makes the session testable with a fake target.

nodes.name: ApprovedWindowStatesTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 tests pinning the approved-vocabulary tables: unique ids, non-empty descriptions, tool names drawn from the known list, arrangement/presentation consistency, and lookup behaviour for unknown names.

nodes.summary: Catch2 tests exercising component lookup and clicking against a real JUCE component tree fixture, covering hidden ancestors, disabled buttons, missing ids, and successful action invocation.

nodes.summary: Catch2 tests for the command parser: valid verbs with and without arguments, blank lines, unknown verbs, missing and extra arguments, and the verb round-trip through commandVerb.

nodes.name: TestControlSessionTests.cpp

nodes.name: states
nodes.summary: Builds and caches the full table of approved window states, each naming the tools it opens, their presentation and arrangement, geometry, microphone and panel flags, and a tester-facing description.

nodes.name: targets
nodes.summary: Builds and caches the table of approved click targets, pairing each wire name with the component id it matches and a description.

nodes.name: approvedWindowStates
nodes.summary: Public accessor returning every window state the application will enter on request.

nodes.name: approvedClickTargets
nodes.summary: Public accessor returning every object the application will allow to be clicked.

nodes.name: findApprovedWindowState
nodes.summary: Looks up a window state by wire name, returning null when the name is not in the approved list so callers treat it as an error.

nodes.name: findApprovedClickTarget
nodes.summary: Looks up a click target by wire name, returning null for unapproved names.

nodes.name: approvedGeometryNames
nodes.summary: Returns the closed list of named window geometries the geometry command accepts.

nodes.name: knownToolNames
nodes.summary: Returns every tool name an approved state may reference; the shell maps these onto ToolType and tests pin the two lists together.

nodes.name: ApprovedWindowState
nodes.summary: Value type describing what the application should look like in an approved state — tools, presentation, arrangement, geometry, microphone and panel flags — rather than the steps to reach it.

nodes.name: ApprovedClickTarget
nodes.summary: Value type pairing an approved click wire name with the component id it addresses and a human-readable description.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Thread body that reads stdin line by line, hands each line to the session on the message thread through a promise/future handshake, prints the rendered response, and exits once the session reports it is finished.

nodes.name: FunctionTestControlTarget
nodes.summary: TestControlTarget implementation that forwards each operation to an injectable std::function, letting the application shell wire up behaviour without defining a subclass.

nodes.name: TestControlChannel
nodes.summary: juce::Thread subclass owning the stdin/stdout command loop and the target it drives; starts on construction and stops cleanly on destruction.

nodes.name: isEffectivelyVisible
nodes.summary: Walks the parent chain up to the root to confirm a component and every ancestor is visible, since juce::Component::isVisible only reports the component's own flag.

nodes.name: clickComponentById
nodes.summary: Finds a component by id and invokes its action, returning false when the object is absent, hidden, disabled, or not clickable so the channel can report an explicit failure.

nodes.name: tokenise
nodes.summary: Splits a command line into whitespace-separated tokens, collapsing runs of separators and emitting the trailing token.

nodes.name: withArgument
nodes.summary: Builds a command that requires exactly one argument, rejecting the line when the argument is missing or an extra token follows.

nodes.name: withoutArguments
nodes.summary: Builds a command that takes no arguments, rejecting the line when any trailing token is present.

nodes.name: parseCommand
nodes.summary: Parses a raw line into a Command, mapping each known verb onto its kind and arity rule and returning an invalid command with a reason for anything unrecognised.

nodes.name: commandVerb
nodes.summary: Maps a CommandKind back to its wire verb, the inverse of the parser's verb table.

nodes.name: Command
nodes.summary: Parsed command value carrying its kind, optional single argument, and an error string populated when the kind is invalid.

nodes.name: renderResponse
nodes.summary: Formats a Response into the channel's line protocol, emitting an OK line with any items or an ERR line carrying the failure reason.

nodes.name: handle
nodes.summary: Dispatches a parsed command: validates state, click, and geometry names against the approved vocabulary before calling the target, serves list-states/list-objects/status queries, and marks the session finished on quit.

nodes.name: handleLine
nodes.summary: Convenience entry point that parses a raw line and immediately handles the resulting command.

nodes.name: Response
nodes.summary: Result of handling a command: a success flag, zero or more result items for discovery and status queries, and an error string on failure.

nodes.name: TestControlSession
nodes.summary: Holds a reference to a TestControlTarget and turns command lines into target calls, exposing isFinished once a quit command has been accepted.

nodes.name: TestControlTarget
nodes.summary: Abstract interface the session drives — apply an approved state, click an approved object, apply a named geometry, report the current state id, and request quit — implemented by the application shell.

nodes.name: Fixture
nodes.summary: Test fixture building a small real JUCE component tree with a title bar and a button, plus a click counter, so clicker behaviour can be asserted without a display.

nodes.name: FakeTarget
nodes.summary: Recording TestControlTarget stub that captures applied states, clicks, and geometries and can be told to refuse each operation, letting session dispatch and failure paths be asserted.

nodes.name: MusicalTime.h
nodes.summary: Defines the score model's fixed musical time base — the signed `Tick` type, the 3840-ticks-per-quarter-note constant, and constexpr conversions from MusicXML/MIDI source durations into that base. Deliberately JUCE-free and dependency-free so it can be shared by both the MusicXML score model and the MIDI timeline.
nodes.languageNotes: Header-only constexpr/noexcept free functions in namespace `score`; integer-only arithmetic avoids floating point so durations compare exactly.

nodes.name: rescaleToTicks
nodes.summary: Converts a source duration denominated in `sourceDivisions` units per quarter note into model ticks, rounding half away from zero and reporting whether the conversion was exact. Non-positive divisions yield zero ticks with `exact == false` rather than dividing by zero.

nodes.name: nominalMeasureTicks
nodes.summary: Computes the tick span of one bar for a given beats/beat-type time signature, returning zero for a malformed signature instead of throwing.

nodes.name: Pitch.h
nodes.summary: Models a notated pitch as spelling (step, alter, octave) plus its sounded MIDI note number, with helpers to derive the number from a spelling, check the two agree (invariant 5), and compare pitches either by spelling or by sound.
nodes.languageNotes: Keeps spelling and sounding pitch as separate facts so enharmonics (F# vs Gb) stay distinguishable while still comparing equal by sound.

nodes.name: semitonesAboveC
nodes.summary: Maps a diatonic step letter to its semitone offset above C within an octave.

nodes.name: Pitch
nodes.summary: Value type holding a notated pitch: diatonic step, chromatic alteration, octave, and the MIDI note number it sounds as.

nodes.name: midiNoteNumberFor
nodes.summary: Derives the sounding MIDI note number from a step/alter/octave spelling.

nodes.name: pitchFromSpelling
nodes.summary: Factory that builds a consistent `Pitch` from a spelling, filling in the MIDI note number so callers cannot construct a contradictory pitch by accident.

nodes.name: isConsistent
nodes.summary: Checks invariant 5 — that a pitch's stored MIDI note number matches the number implied by its spelling.

nodes.name: soundsSameAs
nodes.summary: Compares two pitches by sounding MIDI note number, so enharmonic spellings count as equal.

nodes.name: LyricSyllable.h
nodes.summary: Models one sung syllable attached to a note, carrying verse number, syllabic position within its word, text, and a melisma extender flag so the renderer can draw hyphens and extender lines.

nodes.name: LyricSyllable
nodes.summary: Value type for a single lyric syllable: verse, syllabic position, text, and whether it extends across following notes.

nodes.name: ScoreEvent.h
nodes.summary: Defines the atomic thing that happens in a voice — a note, chord, or rest — with onset, duration, grace flag, tuplet ratio, pitches, tie linkage, and attached lyrics. A chord is one event carrying several pitches rather than several overlapping events.

nodes.name: ScoreEvent
nodes.summary: The core event value type: kind, staff, onset and duration in ticks, grace/tuplet flags, the pitches it sounds, tie references in both directions, and its lyric syllables.

nodes.name: EventRef
nodes.summary: Three-coordinate reference (measure, voice, event index) identifying an event within a part so ties can cross barlines.

nodes.name: TupletRatio
nodes.summary: Actual-in-the-time-of-normal ratio describing an event's tuplet grouping.

nodes.name: ScoreAttributes.h
nodes.summary: Models the notation attributes that can change mid-score — clef, key signature, time signature — plus the per-measure change set and performance directions such as tempo marks and dynamics.

nodes.name: Clef
nodes.summary: A clef assignment: sign, staff line, octave transposition, and which staff it applies to.

nodes.name: KeySignature
nodes.summary: A key signature expressed as MusicXML's signed fifths count plus an optional mode, so sharps and flats stay distinguishable.

nodes.name: TimeSignature
nodes.summary: Beats and beat-type pair defining a measure's nominal length.

nodes.name: AttributeChanges
nodes.summary: The set of clef, key, and time changes declared at one measure; empty for the majority of measures that change nothing.

nodes.name: Direction
nodes.summary: A performance direction attached at an onset — tempo mark, dynamic, or free text — with an optional beats-per-minute rate for metronome marks.

nodes.name: Measure.h
nodes.summary: Defines a measure and the voices inside it: printed number, index, tick start, nominal duration, pickup flag, attribute changes, uninterpreted repeat/jump markings, directions, and per-voice event lists in resolved musical order.

nodes.name: Measure
nodes.summary: One bar of a part: printed number as a string, positional index, tick start and nominal duration, pickup flag, attribute changes, repeat markings, directions, and its voices.

nodes.name: Voice
nodes.summary: One voice's events within a measure in ascending onset order, keyed by MusicXML's voice number rather than a dense index.

nodes.name: RepeatMarkings
nodes.summary: Repeat barlines, repeat counts, ending-bracket numbers, and jump markings captured verbatim as written and deliberately not expanded into a playback order.

nodes.name: Diagnostic.h
nodes.summary: Models what an importer reports about a file it read: a severity (unsupported, repaired, info), a musical rather than textual location, the element name, a message, and an occurrence count for summarised repeats.
nodes.languageNotes: Location fields are all `std::optional` so one type covers document-, part-, measure-, and event-level diagnostics.

nodes.name: Diagnostic
nodes.summary: One importer diagnostic: severity, optional musical location, offending element name, human-readable message, and how many times it occurred.

nodes.name: DiagnosticLocation
nodes.summary: Optional musical coordinates for a diagnostic — part id, printed measure number as a string, voice, and tick position.

nodes.name: TempoMap.h
nodes.summary: Declares the tempo map: ordered tick/BPM entries plus bidirectional conversion between musical position and wall-clock seconds. Deliberately knows nothing about Score/Part/Measure so MIDI import can reuse it, and is explicitly not real-time safe.

nodes.name: TempoMap
nodes.summary: Invariant-enforcing tempo map built through a private constructor plus a static `build` factory; precomputes cumulative seconds per entry so a conversion is a binary search plus one multiply.
nodes.languageNotes: Private constructor + static `build` makes invariant 8 (non-empty, sorted, unique ticks) unconstructably-violable from outside.

nodes.name: TempoEntry
nodes.summary: A tempo declaration: the tick it takes effect at and the quarter-notes-per-minute rate in force until the next entry.

nodes.name: TempoMap.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements the tempo map: sorting and repairing raw entries into invariant 8, precomputing cumulative seconds, and converting ticks to seconds and back by binary search over the entry table.
nodes.languageNotes: Repair-not-reject policy — bad tempi are dropped and a default 120 BPM entry is synthesised, so a malformed file still yields a usable map.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Static factory that enforces invariant 8 on raw entries: drops non-finite or non-positive tempi, stable-sorts by tick, collapses duplicate ticks to the last declaration, and inserts a default 120 BPM entry when nothing covers tick 0.

nodes.name: recomputeCumulativeSeconds
nodes.summary: Rebuilds the per-entry cumulative-seconds table by accumulating each tempo segment's duration, so later conversions need no walk from the top of the score.

nodes.name: beatsPerMinuteAt
nodes.summary: Returns the tempo in force at a tick by binary-searching the entry table for the last entry at or before it.

nodes.name: tickToSeconds
nodes.summary: Converts a musical position to elapsed seconds using the cumulative-seconds table plus the remainder at the governing tempo, so mid-score tempo changes are exact.

nodes.name: secondsToTick
nodes.summary: Inverse of `tickToSeconds`: binary-searches the cumulative-seconds table, rounds to the nearest tick, and clamps times before the start of the score to tick 0.

nodes.name: ticksToSecondsAt
nodes.summary: Computes the wall-clock seconds a tick span occupies at a constant tempo, guarding against unusable BPM values.

nodes.name: Score.h
nodes.summary: Root of the normalized score model — metadata, tick base, parts with their measures and declared divisions, the tempo map, and importer diagnostics — plus helpers for measure count and total length. Engraving-independent by construction and shared across threads as `shared_ptr<const Score>`.
nodes.languageNotes: Immutability is the concurrency strategy: a Score is fully built before first share and never mutated, so `shared_ptr<const Score>` needs no lock. The audio thread never touches it.

nodes.name: Score
nodes.summary: Aggregate root holding metadata, the explicit tick base, all parts, the tempo map, and every diagnostic the importer produced.

nodes.name: Part
nodes.summary: One instrumental or vocal part: the file's verbatim id, display name and abbreviation, staff count, every declared divisions value, and its measures.

nodes.name: ScoreMetadata
nodes.summary: Work and credit metadata from the head of the file, including the encoding software that produced it.

nodes.name: measureCount
nodes.summary: Returns the score's measure count, taken from the first part because invariant 1 requires every part to agree.

nodes.name: totalLength
nodes.summary: Returns the score's total musical length in ticks as the end of its last measure, or zero for an empty score.

nodes.name: MusicalTimeTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 suite covering the tick base and duration rescaling: exact divisibility of common subdivisions, rounding half away from zero, exactness reporting, negative (backup) durations, and malformed divisions or time signatures.

nodes.name: PitchTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 suite pinning pitch semantics: middle C as C4/MIDI 60, A440, octave spacing, double accidentals, enharmonics sounding equal while staying distinguishable, and invariant 5 rejecting a number that contradicts its spelling.

nodes.name: ScoreModelTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Broadest Catch2 suite for the score model, building a two-bar fixture score and asserting measure count, total length, chord-as-one-event, grace notes, tie linkage, repeat markings kept uninterpreted, string measure numbers, lyric verses, clefs, keys, tempo directions, and diagnostics.

nodes.name: makeTwoBarScore
nodes.summary: Test fixture builder assembling a two-measure, single-part score with pitched events so the model assertions have realistic data to run against.

nodes.name: TempoMapTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 suite for tempo-map construction and conversion: the 120 BPM default, linear and multi-segment tick/seconds conversion, invariant-8 repair (sorting, duplicate collapse, dropping meaningless tempi), round-tripping, and clamping times before the score start.

nodes.name: requestJson
nodes.summary: Wraps fetch with JSON parsing and uniform error reporting for every dashboard API call.

nodes.name: index.ts

nodes.name: handlePublicRequest
nodes.summary: Routes the public health, authorization and feedback endpoints and returns 404/405 for anything else.

nodes.name: createAuthorization
nodes.summary: Issues a short-lived signed authorization token for a client installation after version, rate-limit and payload checks.

nodes.name: createSubmission
nodes.summary: Validates, deduplicates, rate-limits, capacity-checks and stores an incoming feedback submission, queuing it for the admin email digest.

nodes.name: readJson
nodes.summary: Reads and size-limits the JSON request body, rejecting wrong content types and malformed payloads.

nodes.name: validateAuthorizationRequest
nodes.summary: Checks an authorization payload's schema version, app version and allowed field set.

nodes.name: validateFeedbackRequest
nodes.summary: Validates a feedback payload: category, message length, contact email, timestamps and optional screenshot attachment.

nodes.name: isRateLimited
nodes.summary: Counts rows for one key column within the trailing hour to decide whether a caller exceeded its quota.

nodes.name: isGlobalRateLimited

nodes.name: verifyToken

nodes.name: compareVersions

nodes.name: notifications.ts
nodes.summary: Claims a batch of queued feedback reports under a per-day email reservation, sends the admin digest, and releases the claim and reservation when configuration is missing or delivery fails.
nodes.languageNotes: The claim/reservation pair is written with atomic SQL (UPDATE ... RETURNING and an ON CONFLICT guarded counter) so concurrent scheduled invocations cannot double-send.

nodes.name: sendPendingFeedbackBatch
nodes.summary: Reserves a daily email slot, claims the oldest queued reports, sends the digest, and rolls the claim back on failure.

nodes.name: feedbackEmailText
nodes.summary: Renders the plain-text digest body listing each claimed report's receipt, category, version and message.

nodes.name: releaseClaim
nodes.summary: Returns a failed batch's rows to the queue by clearing their claim id.

nodes.name: releaseReservation
nodes.summary: Decrements the day's sent counter after a failed send so the slot can be reused.

nodes.name: notificationConfiguration
nodes.summary: Resolves and validates the sender, recipients, dashboard URL and batching limits from the environment bindings.

nodes.name: isEmailAddress
nodes.summary: Performs a conservative structural check that a configured value looks like a single email address.

nodes.summary: Shared operational policy for the worker: storage and retention limits, spam heuristics, request-metric recording, retention sweeps across every table, and the aggregated operational health report.

nodes.name: configuredPositiveInteger

nodes.name: storageLimits

nodes.name: retentionPolicy

nodes.name: estimatedStoredBytes

nodes.name: suspiciousSubmissionReason

nodes.name: checkStorageCapacity

nodes.name: recordRequestMetric
nodes.summary: Upserts the hourly request-metric bucket with counts, outcome and duration for a route.

nodes.name: verifyDatabaseAvailability
