nodes.name: BenchmarkComparability.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements the comparability gate for Performance Lab benchmark runs, field-by-field comparing two BenchmarkRunRecord provenance/configuration values and collecting every material mismatch that would make a comparison meaningless.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a local `display` helper over std::optional to render absent values uniformly, and a repeated `compare` lambda so each mismatch is reported rather than short-circuiting on the first.

nodes.name: BenchmarkComparability.h
nodes.summary: Public interface for benchmark run comparability checking, declaring the mismatch/result value types and the validateComparability entry point over BenchmarkRunRecord pairs.

nodes.name: BenchmarkComparison.cpp
nodes.summary: Computes per-metric absolute and relative median deltas between a baseline and a candidate benchmark run, refusing to calculate anything when the two runs fail the comparability gate.
nodes.languageNotes: Relative percent change is left as an empty std::optional when the baseline value is zero, so callers must distinguish 'no change' from 'undefined change'.

nodes.name: BenchmarkComparison.h
nodes.summary: Declares the metric-level and run-level comparison result structures plus the compareBenchmarkRuns entry point used by the Performance Lab comparison view.

nodes.name: BenchmarkRunner.cpp
nodes.summary: Drives a full benchmark run through its phase machine (validate, stabilize, warm up, measure, aggregate, clean up), collecting trial measurements from a scenario/strategy pair while honouring cancellation and guaranteeing restore/deactivate cleanup.
nodes.languageNotes: Cleanup is funnelled through a single cleanUp path so strategy deactivation and scenario restore still run on cancellation or a thrown exception.

nodes.name: BenchmarkRunner.h
nodes.summary: Declares the benchmark runner phase enum, its progress and result value types, and the BenchmarkRunner class whose collaborators (stabilizer, progress observer, aggregator, cancellation predicate) are injected as std::function callbacks.
nodes.languageNotes: std::function seams instead of virtual interfaces keep the runner unit-testable without a display or a real audio device.

nodes.name: PerformanceLabController.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements the Performance Lab's presentation-independent state machine: inline configuration validation, run start/cancel, history navigation, result selection, comparison, reopening stored runs, and export, each transition publishing a fresh immutable state snapshot.
nodes.languageNotes: Public methods take a mutex and delegate to *Locked helpers, so error reporting cannot deadlock when called from within an already-locked transition.

nodes.name: PerformanceLabController.h
nodes.summary: Declares the Performance Lab view enum, the aggregate PerformanceLabState snapshot, and the controller class that mediates between the UI and the benchmark runner, record loader, and exporter via injected callbacks.
nodes.languageNotes: State is exposed as a whole-value snapshot guarded by a mutex plus an atomic cancellation flag, keeping UI reads consistent while a run executes off the message thread.

nodes.name: BenchmarkComparabilityTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 suite that mutates one provenance/configuration field at a time and asserts validateComparability names each material mismatch, while confirming strategy differences remain intentionally comparable.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Catch2 DYNAMIC_SECTION so each mutated field is reported as its own named section.

nodes.name: BenchmarkComparisonTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 suite covering compareBenchmarkRuns: absolute and relative median deltas, preservation of metrics missing from one side, the zero-baseline case, and refusal to calculate for incomparable runs.

nodes.name: BenchmarkRunnerTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 suite exercising BenchmarkRunner against fake scenarios and strategies, verifying phase progression, warm-up versus measured trials, cancellation handling, and that cleanup runs on every exit path.

nodes.name: PerformanceLabControllerTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 suite driving PerformanceLabController through inline validation, progress reporting with preserved cancelled trials, reopen/export error paths, and blocked comparisons with explained incompatible fields.

nodes.name: validateComparability
nodes.summary: Compares every material provenance and run-configuration field of two benchmark records and returns the full list of mismatches, marking the pair comparable only when no mismatch is found.

nodes.name: ComparabilityMismatch
nodes.summary: Value type naming a single field that differs between two benchmark runs, carrying its rendered baseline and candidate values for display.

nodes.name: ComparabilityResult
nodes.summary: Result of a comparability check: a boolean verdict plus the collected list of field mismatches explaining a negative verdict.

nodes.name: compareBenchmarkRuns
nodes.summary: Builds the per-metric comparison between a baseline and candidate run, computing absolute and relative median change over the union of both metric sets after the comparability gate passes.

nodes.name: MetricComparison
nodes.summary: Per-metric comparison record holding metric id and unit alongside optional baseline/candidate values and the derived absolute and relative changes.

nodes.name: BenchmarkComparisonResult
nodes.summary: Aggregate comparison outcome combining the comparability verdict, any blocking mismatches, and the per-metric comparison rows.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Executes one complete benchmark run: validates scenario and strategy parameters and compatibility, activates the strategy, performs warm-up and measured trials with telemetry, aggregates results, and always restores the scenario on cancellation, failure, or exception.

nodes.name: report
nodes.summary: Updates the runner's current phase and trial counters and notifies the injected progress observer when one is configured.

nodes.name: RunnerProgress
nodes.summary: Snapshot of runner progress: the current phase plus completed and total trial counts for UI display.

nodes.name: BenchmarkRunnerResult
nodes.summary: Outcome of a benchmark run bundling the validation result, the collected trial measurements, the terminal run status, and an optional status detail message.

nodes.name: BenchmarkRunner
nodes.summary: Phase-driven benchmark execution engine that runs a scenario under an optimization strategy, taking its stabilizer, progress observer, aggregator, and cancellation predicate as injected callbacks.

nodes.name: PerformanceLabState
nodes.summary: Immutable snapshot of the entire Performance Lab UI state: active view, configuration and its validation, run progress and flags, safety warnings, run history, selections, comparison result, and any error message.

nodes.name: PerformanceLabController
nodes.summary: Presentation-independent controller owning Performance Lab state transitions, delegating validation, run execution, record loading, and export to injected function seams under a state mutex.

nodes.name: PerformanceLabController
nodes.summary: Constructs the controller from its validator, run executor, record loader, and exporter callbacks and seeds the initial state with a validation pass over the default configuration.

nodes.name: setConfiguration
nodes.summary: Replaces the pending run configuration, re-runs inline validation, and clears any stale error so the configuration view reflects the new input immediately.

nodes.name: startRun
nodes.summary: Blocks invalid configurations, then switches to the live-run view, resets cancellation, invokes the run executor with a progress callback, and appends the resulting record to history.

nodes.name: selectResult
nodes.summary: Selects a history entry by index, rejecting out-of-range indices with an error and otherwise switching the lab to the results view.

nodes.name: selectComparison
nodes.summary: Validates the baseline and candidate history indices, runs compareBenchmarkRuns over the two records, and stores the comparison result while moving to the comparison view.

nodes.name: reopen
nodes.summary: Loads a previously stored benchmark run by identifier through the injected loader, reporting an error when no loader is configured or the load fails, and otherwise appending and selecting the restored record.

nodes.name: exportSelected
nodes.summary: Exports the currently selected run record to a destination via the injected exporter, surfacing missing-selection, missing-exporter, and export-failure conditions as user-visible errors.

nodes.name: comparableRecord
nodes.summary: Test fixture building a fully populated benchmark run record whose provenance and configuration are known-comparable, used as the baseline that each test mutates one field at a time.

nodes.name: recordFor
nodes.summary: Test fixture producing a benchmark run record for a given run id, strategy id, and median value so controller history, selection, and comparison paths can be driven deterministically.

nodes.name: validConfiguration
nodes.summary: Test fixture returning a run configuration that passes the controller's inline validator, used as the baseline for valid-path controller tests.

nodes.name: WorkspaceSplitPane.h
nodes.summary: Header-only JUCE component representing one two-way split in the fractal workspace tree: two child panes separated by a draggable divider that reports its ratio back to the layout model. It is a pure presentation container -- it holds raw pointers to its children and never owns the tool components it displays.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses juce::StretchableLayoutManager plus a private ReportingResizerBar subclass to convert divider drags into a normalised ratio callback.

nodes.name: WorkspaceSplitPane
nodes.summary: juce::Component that lays out exactly two direct children with a draggable divider, enforcing minimum pane sizes and emitting the current split ratio via an onRatioChanged callback. Children may themselves be split panes or tab groups, which is how the workspace subdivides to arbitrary depth.

nodes.name: WorkspaceTabBarButton.h
nodes.summary: Header-only custom tab button that paints the workspace tab strip styling and turns a drag past the threshold (or Ctrl-drag) into a workspace tool drag. Makes tab labels an equal drag source alongside dock headers and floating window title bars.

nodes.name: WorkspaceTabBarButton
nodes.summary: juce::TabBarButton subclass with custom paintButton rendering and mouseDown/mouseDrag/mouseUp handling that arms, starts, and completes a tool drag without disturbing normal tab selection clicks.

nodes.name: WorkspaceTabbedComponent.h
nodes.summary: Header-only juce::TabbedComponent specialisation that builds WorkspaceTabBarButton tabs and maps each tab back to a WorkspaceLayoutState::Tool. It only reparents tool components into tabs -- ownership of the live tool stays with MainComponent, so retabbing never destroys analysis state.
nodes.languageNotes: addToolTab() records the per-tab drag handler before calling addTab(), because juce::TabbedComponent::addTab invokes createTabButton() synchronously.

nodes.name: WorkspaceTabbedComponent
nodes.summary: Tabbed presentation container that tracks the Tool behind each tab, restores the active tool without firing selection callbacks, and reports genuine user tab changes through onActiveToolChanged.

nodes.name: WorkspaceLayoutState.h
nodes.summary: Pure, JUCE-free binary-tree model of the workspace tiling arrangement (bspwm/i3 style): leaves are single tools or tab groups, internal nodes are two-way splits, and drops on pane edges subdivide indefinitely. Deliberately split out of the Component layer so the full insert/remove/validate logic is unit-testable headlessly.
nodes.languageNotes: Header-only, dependency-free C++20 with std::unique_ptr-owned nodes and a self-check validateNode() that guards against duplicate tools or malformed subtrees after every mutation.

nodes.name: WorkspaceLayoutState
nodes.summary: The workspace tiling engine: owns the node tree and exposes insert/remove/split-ratio/active-tab mutations plus arrange-workspace commands, with opaque Tool ids so it has no knowledge of any concrete tool roster.

nodes.name: insert
nodes.summary: Inserts a tool into the tree relative to a target pane and drop zone, either joining the target's tab group (centre) or splitting that pane in the requested direction.

nodes.name: removeRec
nodes.summary: Recursively removes a tool from a subtree, collapsing emptied tab groups and promoting the surviving sibling of a split so the tree never keeps degenerate one-child nodes.

nodes.name: validateNode
nodes.summary: Recursively checks a node's structural invariants -- correct child arity per kind, in-range split ratios, an active tab that exists, and no tool appearing twice anywhere in the tree.

nodes.name: dropZoneForPosition
nodes.summary: Maps a pointer position within a pane's bounds onto a DropZone (left/right/top/bottom edge band or centre), giving the drag-and-drop layer its edge-split hit testing without any JUCE dependency.

nodes.name: convertToSplit
nodes.summary: Replaces a node in place with a new split node whose children are the original node and a leaf for the incoming tool, ordered according to the drop zone.

nodes.name: flattenToTabs
nodes.summary: Collapses the whole tree into a single tab group containing every currently tiled tool, backing the 'tabbed' arrange-workspace command.

nodes.name: collectLeaves
nodes.summary: Walks a subtree in order and appends every tool it finds, in leaves and tab groups alike, to the output vector.

nodes.name: applyLayoutCommand
nodes.summary: Applies a root-level arrange command (horizontal, vertical, or tabbed) to the whole workspace rather than to one targeted pane.

nodes.name: makeSplitNode
nodes.summary: Factory that builds a split node from an orientation, ratio, and two owned child subtrees.

nodes.name: WorkspaceSnapshotCapture.h
nodes.summary: Pure serialisation-side helper that converts the live layout tree plus per-tool observations (presentation, floating bounds, settings payload) into a persistable WorkspaceSnapshot document. Kept JUCE-free so workspace save/restore can be tested without a display.

nodes.name: WorkspaceSnapshotCapture
nodes.summary: Stateless capture utility exposing a ToolObservation input struct and a static capture() entry point that produces a WorkspaceSnapshot from the current layout and tool states.

nodes.name: capture
nodes.summary: Builds a WorkspaceSnapshot by recursively encoding the docked layout tree and collecting the floating tools and focused-tool marker from the supplied observations.

nodes.name: captureNode
nodes.summary: Recursively translates one WorkspaceLayoutState node into its WorkspaceNode document form, skipping tools that are not currently docked and dropping nodes that end up empty.

nodes.name: WorkspaceToolState.h
nodes.summary: Tiny dependency-free state machine tracking one tool's presentation (closed/docked/floating) and an instance generation counter. It encodes the architectural invariant that dock/float moves reparent rather than recreate: the generation only advances when a closed tool is reopened.

nodes.name: WorkspaceToolState
nodes.summary: Presentation state machine returning a Transition struct that tells callers whether the presentation changed and whether a new tool instance is required.

nodes.name: present
nodes.summary: Moves the tool to a target presentation, bumping the instance generation only when it was previously closed so docked/floating transitions preserve the live analysis instance.

nodes.name: MainComponentWorkspaceLayout.cpp
nodes.summary: The MainComponent partial that materialises the abstract WorkspaceLayoutState tree into real JUCE components -- split panes, tabbed groups, and docked tool panels -- and tears them down again on rebuild. It creates and owns only the containers; the tool components themselves remain owned by MainComponent and are merely reparented.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses juce::Component::SafePointer in the ratio/active-tab lambdas so container callbacks stay safe if MainComponent is destroyed, and explicitly clears TabbedComponent tabs before teardown to avoid the tabs deleting borrowed tool components.

nodes.name: buildWorkspaceNode
nodes.summary: Recursively turns a WorkspaceLayoutState node into JUCE components: leaves resolve to the tool's dock, tabs nodes become a WorkspaceTabbedComponent, and splits become a WorkspaceSplitPane wrapping the two recursively built children, with all new containers stored in workspaceContainers.

nodes.name: detachWorkspaceContainer
nodes.summary: Tears down the current container tree, explicitly removing tabs and reparenting docked tool panels first so that destroying the containers never destroys the borrowed tool components.

nodes.name: rebuildWorkspaceContainer
nodes.summary: Detaches the existing container tree, rebuilds it from the current layout state root, attaches the new root, and triggers a relayout.

nodes.name: dockedTools
nodes.summary: Returns every tool type currently in the docked presentation that also has a live dock panel, used as the roster for layout and snapshot work.

nodes.name: layoutWorkspace
nodes.summary: Sets the workspace root component's bounds and relies on JUCE's setBounds/resized cascade to lay out every nested split pane and tab group below it.

nodes.name: setWorkspaceLayout
nodes.summary: Applies an arrange-workspace command to the layout state and rebuilds the container tree to match.

nodes.name: WorkspacePresentationComponentsTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 tests for the workspace presentation containers, checking that WorkspaceSplitPane restores and reports its divider ratio and that WorkspaceTabbedComponent maps tabs back to their tools without spurious selection callbacks.

nodes.name: WorkspaceLayoutStateTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Extensive Catch2 suite exercising the tiling engine headlessly: drop-zone hit testing, edge splits, tab grouping, removal and sibling promotion, arrange commands, and tree-invariant validation.

nodes.name: WorkspaceSnapshotCaptureTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 tests for WorkspaceSnapshotCapture, using a small observe() helper to assert that captured snapshots encode the docked tree, floating tools, and focused tool correctly.

nodes.name: WorkspaceToolStateTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 tests pinning the presentation state machine's central invariant: dock and float transitions keep the same instance generation, and only reopening a closed tool requires a new instance.

nodes.name: PitchDetector.h
nodes.summary: Declares the tuner's allocation-free PitchDetector: a fixed 4096-sample analysis window, a Result carrying detected frequency plus input level, and all FFT/autocorrelation scratch buffers owned as fixed-size std::array members.
nodes.languageNotes: All scratch storage is compile-time sized (std::array, constexpr fftOrder) so a detection frame performs zero heap allocation, matching the project's bounded-analysis contract.

nodes.name: PitchDetector
nodes.summary: Final class computing normalized autocorrelation pitch detection in O(N log N) via a JUCE FFT, owning its FFT input/output, cumulative-energy and correlation buffers so repeated detection is allocation-free.

nodes.name: PitchDetector.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements FFT-accelerated normalized autocorrelation pitch detection with RMS gating, a 16.35 Hz-2500 Hz search range, a minimum correlation score, and parabolic peak refinement. Runs on the message thread from the tuner's timer, never on the audio callback.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses std::span<const float, windowSize> to accept a statically sized frame, letting the compiler prove the buffer length without a runtime check.

nodes.name: detect
nodes.summary: Computes input RMS, gates out silence, then derives the normalized autocorrelation from an FFT power spectrum and picks the best lag above the correlation threshold to report a frequency.

nodes.name: HarmonicAnalyzer.h
nodes.summary: Declares HarmonicAnalyzer and its Result struct (fundamental, spectral centroid, confidence, inharmonicity, input level, pitched flag, and eight relative harmonic amplitudes), reusing PitchDetector's window size and detection.

nodes.name: HarmonicAnalyzer
nodes.summary: Final class that composes a PitchDetector with a Hann-windowed 4096-point JUCE FFT to measure the first eight harmonics of a sustained tone, owning all scratch buffers inline.

nodes.name: HarmonicAnalyzer.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements harmonic analysis: detects the fundamental with PitchDetector, takes a Hann-windowed magnitude spectrum, samples the first eight harmonic partials, and derives spectral centroid, confidence and inharmonicity.

nodes.name: analyze
nodes.summary: Analyzes one fixed-size frame: runs pitch detection, performs a frequency-only forward FFT on the windowed samples, normalizes the eight harmonic amplitudes against the strongest partial, and computes spectral centroid and inharmonicity.

nodes.name: SustainedAudioAnalysisScenario.h
nodes.summary: Declares the Performance Lab benchmark scenario for sustained audio analysis plus the SustainedAudioAnalysisActions abstraction that decouples the scenario from real DSP so it can be unit tested with a fake.
nodes.languageNotes: The pure-virtual actions interface is the project's testability pattern: benchmark policy stays free of JUCE and real FFT work.

nodes.name: SustainedAudioAnalysisActions
nodes.summary: Pure-virtual seam describing the four operations a sustained-analysis benchmark needs: prepare, analyze N frames, report pitched-frame count, and restore.

nodes.name: SustainedAudioAnalysisScenario
nodes.summary: Final BenchmarkScenario implementation that drives a configurable number of sustained-analysis frames (default 64) through an injected actions object.

nodes.name: SustainedAudioAnalysisScenario.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements the sustained-audio benchmark scenario lifecycle: identity accessors, run-configuration validation, prepare/runTrial/restore delegation to the actions seam, and a correctness check that every analyzed frame was detected as pitched.

nodes.name: validate
nodes.summary: Checks a run configuration against the scenario, accumulating human-readable issues for mismatched scenario id, workload id, or missing/empty required fields.

nodes.name: verifyCorrectness
nodes.summary: Post-trial correctness gate: succeeds only when the actions reported a pitched frame for every frame the trial analyzed, otherwise returns a failure result.

nodes.name: HarmonicAnalysisActions.h
nodes.summary: Declares the production implementation of SustainedAudioAnalysisActions, wiring a real HarmonicAnalyzer and a synthetic fixture buffer into the Performance Lab benchmark scenario.

nodes.name: HarmonicAnalysisActions
nodes.summary: Final SustainedAudioAnalysisActions implementation owning a HarmonicAnalyzer, a window-sized fixture buffer, the sample rate (default 48 kHz), and a running pitched-frame count.

nodes.name: HarmonicAnalysisActions.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements the benchmark actions: synthesizes a deterministic harmonic-rich fixture signal, repeatedly runs HarmonicAnalyzer over it counting pitched results, and resets state on restore.

nodes.name: analyzeFixture
nodes.summary: Runs the harmonic analyzer over the prepared fixture for the requested number of frames, incrementing the pitched-frame counter for each result flagged as pitched.

nodes.name: generateFixture
nodes.summary: Fills the fixture buffer with a deterministic multi-partial sine sum so every benchmark trial analyzes identical, reliably pitched input.

nodes.name: PitchDetectorTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 suite for PitchDetector, comparing the FFT implementation against an in-test scalar reference autocorrelation across generated sine waves and including opt-in benchmarks.
nodes.languageNotes: Keeps a naive O(N^2) scalar reference alongside the optimized FFT path so the two can be asserted equivalent — an oracle test rather than a golden-value test.

nodes.name: sineWave
nodes.summary: Test helper generating a fixed-size sine wave buffer at a given frequency and sample rate.

nodes.name: scalarReference
nodes.summary: Naive direct-summation normalized autocorrelation used as the correctness oracle for the production FFT-based detector.

nodes.name: HarmonicAnalyzerTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 suite exercising HarmonicAnalyzer with synthesized multi-partial tones and noise, asserting fundamental detection, relative harmonic amplitudes and pitched/unpitched classification.

nodes.name: harmonicSignal
nodes.summary: Builds an analysis-window-sized buffer summing four harmonic partials at caller-specified amplitudes, giving tests a known harmonic profile to assert against.

nodes.name: SustainedAudioAnalysisScenarioTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 suite covering the sustained-audio benchmark scenario's validation, lifecycle delegation and correctness verification using a fake actions double instead of real DSP.

nodes.name: FakeAnalysisActions
nodes.summary: Test double implementing SustainedAudioAnalysisActions, recording prepare/restore calls and accumulating analyzed and pitched frame counts so scenario behavior can be asserted without running FFTs.

nodes.name: config.py
nodes.summary: Central configuration constants for the roadmap tool: repository coordinates, GitHub Project title/description, the five roadmap stages, status/field option vocabularies, saved view specs, and title-pattern heuristics.

nodes.name: discovery.py

nodes.name: github.py

nodes.name: main.py
nodes.summary: CLI orchestrator for the roadmap tool: parses arguments, runs the full setup pipeline (discover, plan, create project, add issues, provision and assign fields, link sub-issues, ensure views) with threaded progress reporting and cache-backed change detection, then prints a report.

nodes.name: list_all_issues
nodes.summary: Pages through the repository's issues over the GitHub GraphQL API, following cursors until exhausted, and converts each node into an Issue with milestone and native parent metadata.

nodes.name: GitHubError
nodes.summary: Exception raised when a `gh` CLI invocation fails or returns unparsable output.

nodes.name: Project
nodes.summary: Value object identifying a GitHub Project by node id, number, and URL.

nodes.name: GitHubClient
nodes.summary: Client that drives the `gh` CLI to run preflight checks, list issues, create or find the roadmap Project, add and enumerate project items, provision single-select/date/iteration fields, set field values, link sub-issues, and create saved views.

nodes.name: _normalize_field_value
nodes.summary: Normalizes a project field value into a stable comparable string, hashing dicts and joining lists so fingerprints stay deterministic.

nodes.name: parse_args
nodes.summary: Defines and parses the CLI argument surface, including job count, cache path, force/reset flags, and state clearing.

nodes.name: configure_fields
nodes.summary: Provisions the roadmap Project's custom fields (Stage, Priority, Estimate, Target window, dates, iteration) and returns the refreshed field list.

nodes.name: _add_one_issue
nodes.summary: Adds a single issue to the Project via the GitHub API and returns the resulting ProjectItem.

nodes.name: add_issues_with_progress
nodes.summary: Adds all newly selected issues to the Project in parallel with a progress bar, then re-reads project items to reconcile state.

nodes.name: _desired_field_values
nodes.summary: Computes the target field values (stage, priority, estimate, status, dates, target window) for a planned issue, optionally preserving an existing status.

nodes.name: _field_fingerprint
nodes.summary: Builds a stable hash of a project item's desired field state so unchanged issues can be skipped on later runs.

nodes.name: _apply_fields_for_issue
nodes.summary: Applies the desired single-select and date field values for one project item, skipping values already correct and collecting per-field failures.

nodes.name: assign_fields
nodes.summary: Assigns all computed field values across project items in parallel, consulting and updating the fingerprint cache to skip API calls for unchanged issues and summarizing cached/current/API/failed counts.

nodes.name: ensure_subissues_with_progress
nodes.summary: Links each planned issue to its parent as a GitHub sub-issue in parallel, reporting progress and collecting failures.

nodes.name: setup
nodes.summary: Runs the full roadmap pipeline end to end: preflight, issue discovery, descendant selection, planning, project creation, item addition, field provisioning and assignment, sub-issue linking, view creation, and reconciliation into a SetupResult.

nodes.name: print_report
nodes.summary: Prints the human-readable summary of a setup run, including counts, cache hits, and any failures.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point that parses args, acquires the state lock, optionally clears the cache, runs setup, and prints the report.

nodes.name: FieldAssignmentSummary
nodes.summary: Summary of a field-assignment pass: failed updates plus cached, already-current, and API-touched issue counts.

nodes.name: SetupResult
nodes.summary: Aggregate result of a full setup run, carrying the project, discovery/selection counts, missing and duplicate items, failures, field summary, job count, and state path.

nodes.name: models.py
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass models shared across the roadmap tool: Issue, Stage, ProjectItem, and PlannedIssue.

nodes.name: planning.py
nodes.summary: Pure planning logic that turns discovered issues into a scheduled roadmap: parses parent/dependency references from issue bodies, infers stage, priority, estimate and status, topologically orders work, and assigns start/target dates within stage windows.
nodes.languageNotes: Dependency scheduling is a Kahn-style topological sort with a deterministic tiebreak, so runs are reproducible.

nodes.name: progress.py
nodes.summary: Terminal progress bar with ETA estimation, TTY detection, and non-interactive fallback, used to report long-running GitHub operations.

nodes.name: state.py
nodes.summary: On-disk state store for the roadmap tool: caches per-project field-assignment fingerprints under the XDG cache root, supports pruning and clearing, performs atomic saves, and guards concurrent runs with a PID-aware lock file.
nodes.languageNotes: Atomic writes via tempfile + os.replace, and a stale-lock reaper that checks whether the recorded PID is still alive.

nodes.name: Issue
nodes.summary: Immutable representation of a GitHub issue: number, node id, title, body, URL, state, milestone title, and native parent number.

nodes.name: Stage
nodes.summary: Roadmap stage definition with display name, tracker title prefix, target window label, and duration in weeks.

nodes.name: ProjectItem
nodes.summary: A GitHub Project item linking an item id to its issue number and current field values.

nodes.name: PlannedIssue
nodes.summary: An issue after planning, carrying its assigned stage, parent, dependencies, priority, estimate, status, and start/target dates.

nodes.name: next_monday
nodes.summary: Returns the next Monday on or after the given date, used as the roadmap start anchor.

nodes.name: parent_map
nodes.summary: Builds a mapping from issue number to parent issue number using native parents and body references.

nodes.name: descendants_of
nodes.summary: Breadth-first traversal collecting every descendant of a root issue from the parent map.

nodes.name: tracker_stage
nodes.summary: Matches an issue title against configured stage tracker prefixes to identify tracker issues.

nodes.name: stage_for_issue
nodes.summary: Determines an issue's roadmap stage by walking up its parent chain and falling back to milestone-based inference.

nodes.name: estimate_size
nodes.summary: Parses an effort estimate from the issue body and buckets it into an XS-XL t-shirt size.

nodes.name: priority_for
nodes.summary: Derives an issue's priority from critical title patterns, tracker status, and dependency load.

nodes.name: status_for
nodes.summary: Maps an issue's GitHub state and title conventions onto the project's status vocabulary.

nodes.name: stage_ranges
nodes.summary: Computes the calendar start/end date range for each roadmap stage from the roadmap start date.

nodes.name: _topological_order
nodes.summary: Kahn-style topological sort over issue dependencies with a deterministic priority tiebreak, appending any cycle members at the end.

nodes.name: plan_issues
nodes.summary: Core planner that groups issues by stage, topologically orders them by dependency, and allocates start and target dates within each stage window, returning PlannedIssue records.

nodes.name: _format_duration
nodes.summary: Formats a duration in seconds as a compact human-readable h/m/s string for progress ETAs.

nodes.name: ProgressBar
nodes.summary: Stateful terminal progress bar tracking completion, smoothed per-item rate, and ETA, rendering in place on a TTY and degrading to plain lines otherwise.

nodes.name: StateLockError
nodes.summary: Raised when another roadmap run already holds the state lock.

nodes.name: stable_hash
nodes.summary: Produces a deterministic SHA-256 hex digest of an arbitrary JSON-serializable value for change detection.

nodes.name: _cache_root
nodes.summary: Resolves the cache directory from an explicit override, XDG_CACHE_HOME, or the platform default home cache path.

nodes.name: _pid_is_running
nodes.summary: Checks whether a recorded lock-holder PID is still alive so stale locks can be reclaimed.

nodes.name: StateStore
nodes.summary: JSON-backed cache of per-project field fingerprints with load/clear/prune operations, atomic saves via tempfile plus os.replace, and a context-managed PID-aware lock file.

nodes.name: __main__.py
nodes.summary: CLI entry point for the manual GUI verification harness: parses --quick/--full/--geometry-sweep/--check flags, launches the test-control-enabled binary through ApplicationDriver, runs the Textual session, and writes the JSON plus Markdown run record.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses sys.path.insert on the package directory so sibling modules import flatly, and defers the Textual-dependent `app` import until after --check so the harness self-test runs without the optional dependency.

nodes.name: app.py
nodes.summary: Textual terminal UI for a manual verification run, rendering one question at a time and feeding typed lines back into the Session. Deliberately thin — all sequencing decisions live in session.py.
nodes.languageNotes: Answers are typed lines rather than hotkeys because bare letters were swallowed by the note field and F-keys are intercepted by terminal hosts such as VS Code.

nodes.name: driver.py
nodes.summary: Speaks the stdin/stdout test-control protocol to a running Practice Takes process, launching it and issuing list-states, open-state, restart, status and geometry commands. Standard library only so it is testable without Textual.
nodes.languageNotes: Replies terminate with an explicit `ok`/`error ...` verdict line so a reader knows a reply is complete without byte counting or timeouts.

nodes.name: record.py
nodes.summary: Defines the record a manual verification run produces — Answer and Run dataclasses with validation rules — and serialises it to both diffable JSON and a human-readable Markdown summary under the repository's manual-runs directory.
nodes.languageNotes: Enforces honesty invariants in data rather than UI: a failure requires a note, an interrupted run is marked incomplete, and the mode plus geometry sweep are recorded so a quick run cannot be mistaken for a release check.

nodes.name: session.py
nodes.summary: Headless sequencing core of a verification run: parses typed command lines into Entry values and walks the planned Steps, applying answers, area-wide verdicts, skips and unreachable-surface handling into the Run record.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure logic split away from the Textual layer so the whole run flow is unit-testable without a display or a built binary — the same testability split the C++ side uses for WorkspaceLayoutState.

nodes.name: surfaces.py
nodes.summary: Declarative catalogue of the application surfaces the manual harness verifies — each an approved window state plus questions — with helpers to build the run plan per mode and geometry sweep, and a self-validating consistency check.
nodes.languageNotes: Every surface is scored on the same three fixed axes so runs stay comparable across versions; surface-specific extras are recorded separately so they do not dilute that core.

nodes.name: test_manual_gui.py
nodes.summary: Unittest suite covering the display-free parts of the manual GUI harness — surface list coherence, protocol reply parsing, record validation and session sequencing — plus an optional headless Textual UI suite skipped when Textual is absent.
nodes.languageNotes: TerminalUiTests uses IsolatedAsyncioTestCase with Textual's headless pilot and is gated behind skipUnless, so the suite still runs in the ordinary Python test run without the optional dependency.

nodes.name: current_commit
nodes.summary: Returns the short HEAD commit hash for stamping the run record, falling back to "unknown" when git is unavailable or fails.

nodes.name: run_check
nodes.summary: Self-test mode that starts the application, lists its approved states and confirms every surface the harness expects is reachable — proving the harness can drive the binary without asking a person anything.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Parses command-line arguments, validates the surface list, builds the Run and Session, wires a surface-move callback onto the driver, runs the Textual app and writes the resulting record to disk.

nodes.name: VerificationApp
nodes.summary: Textual App that presents the current step, accepts a typed verdict line per question, advances the application to the next surface via a move callback, and adapts its layout by shedding the legend on short terminals.

nodes.name: parse_reply
nodes.summary: Turns raw test-control reply lines into a Reply verdict plus item payload, treating a reply with no ok/error verdict line as a failure.

nodes.name: ApplicationDriver
nodes.summary: Launches the test-control-enabled binary as a subprocess and exposes the control channel as methods — start, stop, list_states, open_state, status, restart and set_geometry — raising ChannelError when a command is refused.

nodes.name: missing_states
nodes.summary: Reports which required surface states the running application does not offer, so harness drift against ApprovedWindowStates is detected before a run starts.

nodes.name: Answer
nodes.summary: Dataclass holding one recorded verdict for a surface/state/geometry/question, with a problems() check rejecting unknown verdicts and failures that carry no note.

nodes.name: Run
nodes.summary: Dataclass for a whole verification run — commit, platform, audio device, mode, geometry sweep and answers — exposing failure collection, waiver handling and aggregate problem reporting.

nodes.name: to_markdown
nodes.summary: Renders a Run as the Markdown summary a person reads, escaping pipes in notes so a note cannot break the results table and marking incomplete runs prominently.

nodes.name: record_paths
nodes.summary: Computes the dated JSON and Markdown output paths for a run, encoding the mode in the filename so a quick run is distinguishable on disk.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Writes both the JSON and Markdown forms of a run into the records directory and returns the two paths.

nodes.name: parse_entry
nodes.summary: Interprets one typed harness line into an Entry action — pass, fail with reason, skip, area pass/skip, unreachable, help or stop — rejecting a failure that carries no reason.

nodes.name: Step
nodes.summary: One planned question in the run — its surface, geometry and question — with a helper indicating whether it is the first step of a new surface, which is when the application must be moved.

nodes.name: Session
nodes.summary: Walks the planned steps for a mode and sweep, recording each answer into the Run and supporting whole-surface pass/skip/fail, unreachable surfaces that fail without abandoning the run, and early finish on stop.

nodes.name: Surface
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass describing one thing a tester looks at: the approved application state to open, its title, the modes that include it, optional extra questions and whether the geometry sweep applies.

nodes.name: surfaces_for_mode
nodes.summary: Returns the surfaces included in a run mode, rejecting an unknown mode rather than silently producing an empty run.

nodes.name: geometries_for_surface
nodes.summary: Decides which window geometries a given surface is repeated at, exempting surfaces that are themselves about window sizing from the sweep.

nodes.name: plan
nodes.summary: Expands a mode and sweep flag into the ordered list of (surface, geometry) pairs a session walks.

nodes.name: validate
nodes.summary: Self-checks the declarative surface list for duplicate states, malformed entries, and the invariant that quick mode is a strict subset of full, returning a list of problems.

nodes.name: required_states
nodes.summary: Lists every approved application state the surface catalogue depends on, so the harness can check the running binary offers them all before starting.

nodes.name: SurfaceListTests
nodes.summary: Tests that the surface catalogue is coherent — quick mode is a strict subset of full and stays small, every surface asks the three fixed axes first, and the geometry sweep is off by default and skips size-exempt surfaces.

nodes.name: MissingStateTests
nodes.summary: Tests that missing_states reports nothing when the application offers every required state and detects a harness that has drifted from the approved state list.

nodes.name: ReplyParsingTests
nodes.summary: Tests the test-control reply grammar: success with and without payload items, failure carrying its reason, and a verdict-less reply being treated as a failure.

nodes.name: RecordTests
nodes.summary: Tests the run record's honesty rules — failures need notes, incomplete runs say so prominently, mode and geometry sweep are recorded and encoded in the filename, pipes in notes do not break the table, and JSON round-trips.

nodes.name: SessionTests
nodes.summary: Tests session sequencing without a display: every question of every surface is walked, the sweep multiplies steps, a note-less failure does not advance, the application moves only on surface change, and area verdicts stop at the surface boundary.

nodes.name: TerminalUiTests
nodes.summary: Drives the real Textual UI headlessly to verify typed commands, refusal of a reasonless failure, area pass/skip, quitting recording an incomplete run, and the layout shedding its legend on a small terminal.

nodes.name: NamedWorkspaceService.h
nodes.summary: Header-only policy service for named window layouts: saves, applies, renames, overwrites and deletes entries in a WorkspaceCatalog, returning a status result instead of touching UI. Enforces name validation, reserved built-in names, a 128-workspace cap and unique id generation.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure C++ policy class with no JUCE dependency, so the whole save/rename/delete state machine is unit-testable without a display; all mutations return [[nodiscard]] Result values carrying a ResultStatus enum.

nodes.name: NamedWorkspaceService
nodes.summary: Stateless-by-design service class owning the rules for named workspaces, parameterised by an injectable IdGenerator. Exposes save/apply/rename/overwrite/remove plus private name-normalisation and lookup helpers.

nodes.name: save
nodes.summary: Saves the current layout under a new name, rejecting invalid or reserved names, requiring confirmation on a name collision, and failing when the catalog is full or no unique id can be generated.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Activates a workspace by id, resolving it first against the built-in presets and then against the catalog's named entries, and marking it as the catalog's active source.

nodes.name: rename
nodes.summary: Renames a named workspace after validating the new name, refusing built-in ids, and asking for confirmation when the name collides with another saved entry (replacing it in place).

nodes.name: overwrite
nodes.summary: Replaces the stored snapshot of an existing named workspace with the current layout, requiring explicit confirmation and rejecting immutable built-ins.

nodes.name: remove
nodes.summary: Deletes a named workspace after confirmation, erasing it from the catalog and clearing the active source when the deleted entry was selected.

nodes.name: defaultIdGenerator
nodes.summary: Builds the default IdGenerator, a closure over a seeded random engine that emits zero-padded hexadecimal workspace ids.

nodes.name: prepareName
nodes.summary: Normalises a user-supplied workspace name by trimming it, then rejects empty names, names over the 80-character limit and names reserved by built-in presets.

nodes.name: trim
nodes.summary: Strips leading and trailing whitespace from a workspace name using a locale-safe unsigned-char isspace check.

nodes.name: folded
nodes.summary: Produces a lowercase fold of a name so collision and reserved-name checks are case-insensitive.

nodes.name: uniqueId
nodes.summary: Draws ids from the generator until one collides with neither an existing named workspace nor a built-in preset, giving up after a bounded number of attempts.

nodes.name: WorkspaceMenuModel.h
nodes.summary: Defines the JUCE-free view model that drives the workspace section of the Tools menu: a flat list of built-in and named entries plus the enabled/disabled state of Save As, Overwrite, Rename and Delete.
nodes.languageNotes: Plain aggregate structs with a defaulted operator== so menu snapshots can be compared directly in tests.

nodes.name: WorkspaceMenuEntry
nodes.summary: One row of the workspace menu: id, display name, whether it is a built-in preset and whether it is currently active.

nodes.name: WorkspaceMenuModel
nodes.summary: Aggregate holding the ordered workspace menu entries and the four command-availability flags, constructed from a WorkspaceCatalog.

nodes.name: fromCatalog
nodes.summary: Projects a WorkspaceCatalog into a menu model, listing built-in presets before saved workspaces, marking the active source, and enabling Overwrite/Rename/Delete only when the active workspace is a user-saved one.

nodes.name: MainComponentWorkspaceMenu.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements MainComponent's Tools popup menu: per-tool open/dock/float/close submenus, root layout orientation options, the workspace list built from WorkspaceMenuModel, and the save/overwrite/rename/delete/reset workspace commands. Also hosts the optional Performance Lab window entry points.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses juce::Component::SafePointer in the async menu callback so a menu selection arriving after the window closes cannot dereference a destroyed MainComponent.

nodes.name: showToolsMenu
nodes.summary: Builds and shows the whole Tools popup menu, then dispatches the async selection to tool open/present/close calls, layout changes, workspace application, or the workspace save/rename/delete confirmation dialogs.

nodes.name: NamedWorkspaceServiceTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 suite covering NamedWorkspaceService's save, apply, rename, overwrite and delete rules, including reserved built-in names, confirmation-required collisions, catalog capacity limits and injected id generators.

nodes.name: WorkspaceMenuModelTests.cpp
nodes.summary: Catch2 suite asserting that WorkspaceMenuModel::fromCatalog lists built-ins ahead of saved workspaces, flags the active selection, and gates the Overwrite/Rename/Delete commands correctly.

nodes.name: coverage_sources.py
nodes.summary: Parses the root CMakeLists.txt to determine which src/ translation units are compiled into the PracticeTakesTests binary, splitting them into in-test-build, not-in-test-build, and listed-but-absent sets. Supplies the half of a coverage report that gcovr cannot produce: the files no coverage tool can measure at all.
nodes.languageNotes: Standard-library-only Python with regex-based CMake parsing; deliberately raises rather than returning an empty set when the add_executable block is missing, so a parse failure cannot masquerade as a catastrophic coverage finding.

nodes.name: run_coverage.py
nodes.summary: Driver script that configures a dedicated instrumented build tree, builds and runs PracticeTakesTests, then invokes gcovr to emit XML/JSON/HTML coverage reports alongside the test-build membership report from coverage_sources. Coverage is informational — the script never fails on a low number.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses sys.path insertion to import its sibling module; keeps the coverage tree separate from the normal build because instrumented objects are not interchangeable and ccache conflicts with gcov counters.

nodes.name: test_coverage_sources.py
nodes.summary: Unittest suite for coverage_sources covering CMake target parsing, compiled-unit discovery, classification edge cases (headers, missing files, fully covered targets), summary formatting, and two integration checks against the real repository.
nodes.languageNotes: Builds synthetic src/ trees and CMakeLists fixtures in a TemporaryDirectory, then supplements them with assertions run against the actual repository tree.

nodes.name: read_test_target_sources
nodes.summary: Extracts every src/ path listed inside the add_executable(PracticeTakesTests ...) block of a CMakeLists file, excluding paths under src/tests/. Raises ValueError when the block cannot be found so a parsing failure is not mistaken for zero coverage.

nodes.name: find_compiled_sources
nodes.summary: Walks the source root and returns every .cpp translation unit as a repository-relative path, skipping the src/tests/ tree since tests are the measurement rather than the thing measured.

nodes.name: classify
nodes.summary: Core classification entry point: intersects discovered translation units with the CMake test target listing to produce in_test_build, not_in_test_build, and listed_but_absent path lists.

nodes.name: summarise
nodes.summary: Renders a classification dict as a human-readable report giving the in-test-build percentage and naming every source file outside the test binary or listed but missing from disk.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point exposing --source-root, --cmake-lists and --json flags; prints either the JSON classification or the human summary and always returns 0 because the report is informational.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Echoes a command line then executes it via subprocess.run with check=True, used for every external tool invocation in the coverage pipeline.

nodes.name: configure
nodes.summary: Runs CMake configure for the dedicated coverage tree with Debug, BUILD_TESTING and PRACTICE_TAKES_ENABLE_COVERAGE enabled, and explicitly clears the compiler launchers so ccache cannot corrupt gcov counters.

nodes.name: run_tests
nodes.summary: Locates the PracticeTakesTests binary in either the build root or its bin/ subdirectory and executes it with check=False, since gcov counters are written even when the suite fails.

nodes.name: run_gcovr
nodes.summary: Invokes gcovr over the instrumented build tree to emit XML, JSON-summary and HTML-details reports filtered to src/, excluding _deps directories whose HarfBuzz/Ragel generated sources make gcov hard-error. Returns False when gcovr is not installed.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point orchestrating configure, build, test run and gcovr; always writes test-build-membership.json and the membership summary first, then treats a missing gcovr as a warning rather than a failure.

nodes.name: CoverageSourcesTests
nodes.summary: Unittest TestCase with fixture helpers that synthesise src/ trees and CMakeLists files, plus fourteen tests covering target parsing, header handling, absent-file detection, summary text, and real-repository classification invariants.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Two-stage Docker build for the feedback-intake service: a build stage that installs the npm workspace and bundles the worker with esbuild, and a slim runtime stage that runs the bundle as the unprivileged node user on port 8787.
nodes.languageNotes: Multi-stage build keeps devDependencies and the esbuild toolchain out of the runtime image; only /app/feedback-intake/dist is copied forward. Ownership is fixed with chown before dropping to USER node so the container never runs as root.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Build stage on node:26-bookworm-slim that restores the npm workspace lockfile, installs only the @practice-takes/feedback-intake workspace, and runs the build:docker esbuild bundle step.

nodes.name: runtime
nodes.summary: Runtime stage that copies only the compiled dist output plus the entrypoint script, drops privileges to the node user, exposes port 8787, and launches docker-entrypoint.sh.

nodes.name: benchmarks.yml
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions workflow that builds a Release tree on every push to main touching C++ sources (excluding the TypeScript worker under src/services), runs the Catch2 [.benchmark] tag, and probes application startup wall-clock time. Results are formatted into the step summary and uploaded as a 90-day artifact.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a weekly cron baseline alongside path-filtered pushes so the timing series stays continuous even in weeks with no C++ changes.

nodes.name: build-multiplatform.yml
nodes.summary: The desktop packaging workflow: builds, signs, and packages PracticeTakes for Linux (.deb), Windows (NSIS .exe with Authenticode), and macOS (.pkg with Developer ID signing plus notarization), then verifies each package installs and assembles the six installers into a single release-assets bundle with SHA256SUMS and build metadata.
nodes.languageNotes: Exposed as a reusable workflow via workflow_call with individually named optional signing secrets, so a missing certificate degrades to an unsigned build instead of failing the job.

nodes.name: clang-tidy-main.yml
nodes.summary: Post-merge quality workflow that applies safe clang-tidy fix-its and clang-format to merged C++ under src/, revalidates the build, and pushes an automatic fix commit back to main.
nodes.languageNotes: Guards against a self-triggering loop with an actor check on github-actions[bot], and hard-fails when the file discovery glob matches zero .cpp files so an empty analysis cannot report success.

nodes.name: coverage.yml
nodes.summary: Informational coverage workflow with three independent jobs measuring C++ (gcov via run_coverage.py), TypeScript (vitest), and Python coverage, publishing each as a step summary and artifact.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately gate-free: the header documents that no threshold or ratchet is applied because there is no trustworthy baseline yet.

nodes.name: cpp-quality-check.yml
nodes.summary: Pull-request gate that configures a ccache-backed compilation database, builds the app to generate JUCE headers, then enforces clang-format compliance and clang-tidy findings across all non-test C++ sources.
nodes.languageNotes: clang-tidy needs the generated JuceHeader.h, so the workflow must build the app target before linting rather than linting from a bare checkout.

nodes.name: pages.yml
nodes.summary: Publishes the committed .ua/knowledge-graph.json as a static Understand-Anything dashboard site on GitHub Pages, verifying graph provenance and regression first, building the pinned upstream dashboard with pnpm/vite in demo mode, and staging only the three data files the site fetches.
nodes.languageNotes: Never regenerates the graph or calls a model — it reacts only to a regenerated graph being committed, and pins the upstream dashboard by commit SHA because 2.9.4 has no resolvable tag.

nodes.name: python-check.yml
nodes.summary: Runs the standard-library-only Python test suite for the repository tooling and enforces that src/tests/ mirrors the src/ source tree, on both pull requests and pushes to main.
nodes.languageNotes: Path filters include src/** and src/tests/** because the layout check reads both trees, so a misplaced new test must be able to fail this job.

nodes.name: release.yml
nodes.summary: End-to-end release orchestration: a manual-verification gate, version calculation from tools/VERSION, an immutable release commit and tag, a reusable call into the multiplatform build workflow, and publication of the six attested installers as a GitHub release.
nodes.languageNotes: Verifies the downloaded artifact bundle by exact file list, count, SHA256SUMS, and build metadata before attesting provenance — the release cannot publish a bundle it did not fully account for.

nodes.name: secret-scan.yml
nodes.summary: Two-job secret defence: gitleaks scans commit history on pushes, pull requests, and a weekly full-history sweep, while a second job audits tracked files against the repository's own secret-pattern rules.
nodes.languageNotes: Disables gitleaks SARIF artifact upload and PR comments because the report quotes matched secrets verbatim and artifacts on a public repository are world-downloadable.

nodes.name: services-check.yml
nodes.summary: Quality gate for the TypeScript workspace under src/services: runs npm ci, type-check, and the vitest suite, then builds the feedback-intake container image and asserts it runs as a non-root user with a loadable server bundle.
nodes.languageNotes: The separate container-build job exists because the image bundles the dashboard with a workspace-hoisted esbuild, which a dependency update can break without failing the type-check job.

nodes.name: smoke.yml
nodes.summary: Builds the application with the development-only test-control channel enabled and launches it under Xvfb to assert process lifecycle: that it starts, that a tool opens, and that it shuts down cleanly.
nodes.languageNotes: JUCE on Linux needs a real X server, so the run uses xvfb-run rather than an offscreen mode; the suite is kept separate from the unit suite because lifecycle assertions are the classic flake source.

nodes.name: 0001_initial.sql
nodes.summary: Baseline D1 migration creating the feedback-intake schema: authorization request rate-limit log, consumed authorization tokens, and the feedback_submissions table with lookup indexes on installation and client hashes.
nodes.languageNotes: SQLite/D1 dialect: INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT rowid keys and epoch-integer timestamps alongside ISO-text submitted_at.

nodes.name: authorization_requests
nodes.summary: Append-only log of authorization attempts keyed by hashed client identity and request timestamp, used to enforce per-client rate limits.

nodes.name: consumed_authorizations
nodes.summary: Single-use token ledger recording which authorization token ids have already been redeemed, preventing replay of a submission token.

nodes.name: feedback_submissions
nodes.summary: Core table storing every accepted in-app feedback submission — receipt id, schema version, timestamps, app version, hashed installation/client identity, category, message, and optional contact email.
nodes.languageNotes: Extended incrementally by migrations 0002 (triage columns), 0004 (screenshots), 0005 (idempotency key) and 0006 (quarantine).

nodes.name: 0002_admin_triage.sql
nodes.summary: Adds admin triage columns to feedback_submissions — constrained status, developer notes, priority, JSON tags, GitHub issue URL, and a self-referencing duplicate_of link — plus status and category indexes.
nodes.languageNotes: CHECK constraints act as the enum type SQLite lacks; duplicate_of is a self-referencing foreign key back to receipt_id.

nodes.name: 0003_admin_action_receipts.sql
nodes.summary: Creates the admin_action_receipts audit table together with three indexes covering recent-activity, per-admin, and per-receipt lookups.

nodes.name: admin_action_receipts
nodes.summary: Audit trail of administrator create/update/delete actions against a submission receipt, capturing the acting admin email, a JSON details blob, and the action timestamp.

nodes.name: 0004_optional_screenshots.sql
nodes.summary: Adds optional screenshot_mime_type and screenshot_base64 columns to feedback_submissions so clients can attach an inline screenshot with a report.

nodes.name: 0005_idempotent_submissions.sql
nodes.summary: Adds a client_submission_id column and a partial unique index on (installation_hash, client_submission_id), making retried submissions from the same installation idempotent.
nodes.languageNotes: Partial index (WHERE client_submission_id IS NOT NULL) keeps the uniqueness constraint from colliding on legacy rows that predate the column.

nodes.name: 0006_operations.sql
nodes.summary: Operational-visibility migration: adds quarantine columns and a partial index to feedback_submissions, and creates the request_metrics rollup and maintenance_runs history tables.

nodes.name: request_metrics
nodes.summary: Hourly rollup of request counts and latency (total and maximum duration) bucketed by route and outcome, keyed on the (hour, route, outcome) composite primary key.
nodes.languageNotes: Composite primary key makes the hourly bucket an upsert target rather than an append-only event stream.

nodes.name: maintenance_runs
nodes.summary: History of maintenance operations (currently only retention sweeps) recording the actor, start/completion timestamps, and a JSON details payload.

nodes.name: 0007_email_notification_limits.sql
nodes.summary: Introduces the feedback_email_queue with a claim-based pending index, backfills it from existing feedback_submissions, and adds feedback_notification_days to cap daily notification sends.
nodes.languageNotes: Data migration as well as schema migration: an INSERT ... SELECT backfills the queue from existing submissions in the same file.

nodes.name: feedback_email_queue
nodes.summary: Pending-notification work queue holding a denormalized copy of each submission plus claim_id/claimed_at fields so a worker can lease an item before sending the email.

nodes.name: feedback_notification_days
nodes.summary: Per-day counter of notification emails sent, constrained to at most three per day, used to enforce the daily email send budget.

nodes.name: CONTRIBUTING.md
nodes.summary: Contributor entry point that indexes the docs/development/ guides, documents the deliberately minimal repository layout (src/, docs/, openspec/, tools/), and states when a change needs an OpenSpec proposal versus a straight pull request.
nodes.languageNotes: Acts as a hub document: nearly every section is a pointer into docs/development/ rather than duplicated prose, so it stays short while covering build, architecture, quality, and merge policy.

nodes.name: SECURITY.md
nodes.summary: Security policy directing vulnerability reports to GitHub private security advisories rather than public issues, and declaring that only the latest release (per the root VERSION file) is supported while the v0.5.6 LTS branch remains inactive groundwork.

nodes.name: dependabot.yml
nodes.summary: Dependabot configuration running weekly update checks across three ecosystems: GitHub Actions at the repository root, npm at the src/services workspace root (which owns package-lock.json), and Docker inside src/services/feedback-intake.
nodes.languageNotes: The npm directory points at the workspace root rather than the member package, so the shared lockfile stays consistent with every member manifest.

nodes.name: .pre-commit-config.yaml
nodes.summary: Commit gate wiring four local hooks: installing the repository's Git merge drivers, encrypting and staging SOPS secrets, auditing for tracked plaintext secrets, and running clang-format over C/C++ sources.
nodes.languageNotes: Installs both pre-commit and pre-merge-commit hook types; the merge-config and secret-audit hooks run at both stages because Git cannot read merge-driver definitions out of a clone and a merge can otherwise introduce plaintext secrets.

nodes.name: .sops.yaml
nodes.summary: SOPS creation rule binding every .sops file under .secrets/ to a single age recipient key, so encrypted secret mirrors are produced with the right key automatically.

nodes.name: CLAUDE.md
nodes.summary: Six-line root stub that keeps the repository root small by @-importing docs/development/agents/AGENT_GUIDE.md, which holds the actual guidance for coding agents working in this repository.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the Claude Code `@path` import directive so the real guide can live under docs/ while tooling still finds it at the required root location.

nodes.name: CMakeLists.txt
nodes.summary: Root CMake build definition: validates and propagates tools/VERSION, fetches pinned JUCE 8.0.12 and Catch2 v3.8.1, declares the PracticeTakes JUCE GUI app and its full source list, gates the Performance Lab / test-control / coverage options, and builds the PracticeTakesTests Catch2 target.
nodes.languageNotes: Sets VCPKG_MANIFEST_DIR to tools/ before project() because the vcpkg toolchain only auto-discovers a manifest in CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR; Linux builds also apply two in-tree JUCE ALSA patches before the app target is declared.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: User-facing project overview describing the tuner and spectrogram tools, the workspace/docking interface, portable .ptsettings import/export, the feedback flow, packaged platforms, and where developer documentation lives.

nodes.name: pyproject.toml
nodes.summary: Python tooling project definition for practice-takes-tools (not the shipped app): deliberately empty runtime dependencies so pre-commit and CI scripts stay standard-library only, with the Textual manual-GUI harness in a default dependency group and pinned coverage/clang-format tooling behind an optional extra.
nodes.languageNotes: clang-format is pinned to 18.1.8 to match the CI runner after a version drift caused a locally-clean, CI-red tree; run_clang_format.py warns when the installed version differs from this pin.

nodes.name: FEEDBACK.md
nodes.summary: Describes the in-app feedback client's operational contract: the v1 wire schema, the CMake-configurable intake endpoint, the /v1/authorizations then /v1/submissions call sequence, offline draft queuing, and how the six user-facing feedback types collapse onto four wire categories.
nodes.languageNotes: Documents a contract shared across two languages — the C++ client and the TypeScript Worker — which is exactly the drift risk QA_STRATEGY area 12 flags.

nodes.name: MERGING.md
nodes.summary: Explains the repository's opt-in Git merge configuration and the four custom merge drivers (cmake-sources, npm-lock, ours for generated .ua files, union for manual-run records), including why Git forbids defining drivers in a clone and how to bypass or remove them.
nodes.languageNotes: The cmake-sources driver only auto-resolves conflict regions where every line on all three sides is a bare source path — a deliberately conservative rule so a wrongly merged build file cannot parse successfully and fail later.

nodes.name: RELEASING.md
nodes.summary: The release runbook: tools/VERSION is the single source of truth for the version, the Actions workflow tags an immutable release commit then builds and verifies six platform packages, and the document covers artifact provenance plus the not-yet-enabled Windows Authenticode and macOS Developer ID signing secrets.
nodes.languageNotes: Signing steps are already committed but gated on repository secrets that do not exist yet, so each platform can be enabled independently without touching the workflow.

nodes.name: SECRETS.md
nodes.summary: Documents SOPS/age secret management: plaintext secrets stay out of Git while encrypted mirrors under .secrets/ are committed, driven by tools/secret-patterns and secrets_manager.py, with setup, key rotation, daily encrypt/decrypt/sync commands, ciphertext conflict resolution, and the pre-commit hooks' safety behavior.
nodes.languageNotes: Notes that `sops updatekeys` only re-wraps the existing data key, so revoking a recipient additionally requires `sops rotate` and, if the identity leaked, rotating the underlying credentials.

nodes.name: CODE_STYLE.md
nodes.summary: The C++ house style: descriptive naming, intent-explaining comments, RAII/unique_ptr ownership with references for shared services, and the real-time audio rules forbidding allocation, locks, I/O, logging, and FFT work inside the JUCE audio callback.
nodes.languageNotes: Defers all mechanical formatting to .clang-format and static analysis to .clang-tidy, so the prose covers only judgement-level rules a tool cannot enforce.

nodes.name: MANUAL_GUI_VERIFICATION.md
nodes.summary: Documents the interactive manual GUI verification harness — how to build with the test control channel, run it via uv, answer its typed prompts, and how release.yml gates releases on a complete current full-mode run, including skip inputs and waivers.
nodes.languageNotes: The harness never synthesises input events: it names an approved state or object and the application performs the action in process, so a layout change cannot silently redirect a click.

nodes.name: QA_STRATEGY.md
nodes.summary: The living QA gap-closure plan from the July 2026 review, enumerating fourteen numbered areas (TypeScript service CI, cross-platform test execution, supply-chain hygiene, CodeQL, governance docs, performance benchmarking, coverage measurement, untested C++ translation units, worker paths, roadmap tooling, wire-contract conformance, sanitizer builds, macOS tests) with status, dependencies, and suggested sequencing.
nodes.languageNotes: Carries the measured coverage baseline with its caveat: the 89.7% C++ figure covers only the 25 of 43 translation units compiled into PracticeTakesTests, so it must be read alongside coverage_sources.py output.

nodes.name: QUALITY.md
nodes.summary: Sets up the day-to-day quality tooling: pre-commit clang-format and the SOPS secret hooks locally, the clang-tidy auto-fix workflow on main, the check-only pull-request gate, manual clang-tidy invocation, and VS Code IntelliSense configuration via CMake's compilation database.
nodes.languageNotes: Pins the CI clang-format version (18.1.8) because formatter releases disagree at the column limit, so an unpinned local binary can leave a tree clean locally and red in CI.

nodes.name: TEST_LAYOUT.md
nodes.summary: Explains that src/tests/ mirrors src/ so a test's path names the source directory it covers, where non-mirrored fixtures and cross-cutting suites live, and how check_test_layout.py enforces the two layout rules in CI.
nodes.languageNotes: Both src/ and src/tests/ sit on the test target's include path, so tests include their subject by source-relative path and moving a test between directories never breaks its includes.
