nodes.name: .openspec.yaml
nodes.summary: OpenSpec change marker for the musicxml-import proposal, declaring the spec-driven schema and a 2026-07-31 creation date. Its presence is what makes the surrounding directory a recognised OpenSpec change.

nodes.name: proposal.md
nodes.summary: Proposal for a normalized, engraving-independent score model plus a MusicXML importer (.musicxml/.xml/.mxl), arguing the model must land before the renderer so it is not shaped by a paint routine. Declares two new capabilities (normalized-score-model, musicxml-import), the libmusicxml/juce::ZipFile dependency impact, and an explicit non-scope covering rendering, MIDI, playback, and session files.

nodes.name: design.md
nodes.summary: Design document for the score model and MusicXML importer, opening with six decisions escalated to the maintainer and their recorded resolutions: owning layer and namespace, a fixed 3840 PPQ score-wide tick base, as-written-only measure ordering, separate MusicXML/MIDI models sharing one TempoMap, libmusicxml (MPL-2.0) via pinned FetchContent, and a MuseScore-only fixture corpus. Then specifies entities, invariants, ownership/threading rules, the import failure model, and the supported MVP subset.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the OpenSpec convention of a 'Decisions needed from Derek' block that is later answered in a 'Resolved Questions' section, so the rejected alternatives stay readable alongside the choice.

nodes.name: tasks.md
nodes.summary: Ten-section implementation checklist for the musicxml-import change, running from the settled-decisions table through model types, invariants, the parser adapter and .mxl acceptance, importer structure/time/pitch/attributes, the subset boundary and diagnostics, a real-score corpus, and final documentation and verification steps.

nodes.name: .openspec.yaml
nodes.summary: OpenSpec change marker for the real-world-performance-benchmarking proposal, declaring the spec-driven schema and a 2026-07-27 creation date. Its presence is what makes the surrounding directory a recognised OpenSpec change.

nodes.name: proposal.md
nodes.summary: Proposal for a GUI Performance Lab that runs repeatable end-to-end scenarios on physical hardware against a baseline or selected optimization strategy, capturing hardware/build/audio provenance, latency, CPU/memory, and audio-callback stability. Introduces the hardware-performance-lab capability and requires orchestration and telemetry to stay off the real-time audio thread.

nodes.name: design.md
nodes.summary: Design document for the Performance Lab, deciding on declarative scenarios driven by an application-level runner, a stable strategy registry with an always-present baseline, a split between lock-free real-time event capture and non-real-time aggregation, immutable versioned run records exported as JSON, and a three-view (configure / live-run / results) GUI. Records the noise, instrumentation-overhead, and schema-evolution trade-offs plus a six-step migration plan behind a development feature flag.
nodes.languageNotes: The audio-thread section restates the repository-wide hard constraint that the callback must stay constant-time, lock-free, and allocation-free, here applied to instrumentation rather than analysis.

nodes.name: tasks.md
nodes.summary: Six-section implementation checklist covering benchmark contracts and fakes, the scenario runner state machine, real-time and platform metrics/provenance, the strategy registry with comparability and storage, the Performance Lab GUI, and a hardware pilot and acceptance phase. Nearly complete, with the instrumentation-overhead calibration and the end-to-end hardware acceptance run still outstanding.

nodes.name: .env.example
nodes.summary: Template for the operator environment file holding Cloudflare account/API credentials, the D1 database id, dashboard login, Access hostname, and notification sender used by the self-hosted feedback dashboard and the setup scripts.
nodes.languageNotes: CLOUDFLARE_SETUP_API_TOKEN is deliberately separated from the long-lived token so the elevated Access/Workers-write scope can be revoked once setup finishes.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Operator and developer manual for the feedback Worker: public intake protocol, Cloudflare Access-protected admin API surface, triage model, local development, the self-hosted dashboard container, deployment, testing, security controls, retention/recovery, and credential rotation.

nodes.name: compose.yaml
nodes.summary: Docker Compose definition for the single self-hosted `feedback-dashboard` container, building from the service Dockerfile and binding port 8787 to loopback only while requiring every Cloudflare and admin credential to be present.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `${VAR:?message}` mandatory-variable syntax so a missing credential fails at compose time rather than inside the container, and publishes on 127.0.0.1 to keep the admin UI off the network.

nodes.name: docker-entrypoint.sh
nodes.summary: Container entrypoint that fails fast when any required Cloudflare or admin variable is missing, enforces a 16-character minimum admin password, then execs the bundled dashboard server.
nodes.languageNotes: POSIX sh with `set -eu` and `: "${VAR:?msg}"` guards; `exec` hands PID 1 to Node so signals reach the server directly.

nodes.name: package.json
nodes.summary: Workspace manifest for the `@practice-takes/feedback-intake` Worker, defining the typecheck, vitest, wrangler dev/deploy, D1 local/remote migration, and esbuild docker-server bundling scripts along with the Cloudflare toolchain dependencies.
nodes.languageNotes: The `build:docker` esbuild invocation registers text loaders for .html/.css/.js so dashboard assets are inlined into the Node bundle the same way Wrangler's Text rules inline them for the Worker.

nodes.name: tsconfig.json
nodes.summary: TypeScript configuration for the Worker: strict, no-emit ESNext/bundler resolution typechecking over `src/**/*.ts` and `test/**/*.ts` with both Cloudflare Workers and Node type packages loaded.
nodes.languageNotes: Both `@cloudflare/workers-types` and `node` types are included because the same sources run on the Worker runtime and in the Node-hosted dashboard container.

nodes.name: wrangler.example.jsonc
nodes.summary: Template Wrangler configuration declaring the Worker entry module, text-asset rules for the dashboard files, rate/retention/capacity vars, three daily email cron triggers, the send_email binding, and the D1 database binding with its migrations directory.
nodes.languageNotes: All operational policy (per-hour caps, storage ceilings, per-status retention windows, admin route kill switch) is expressed as plain `vars` strings so it can be changed by redeploying config rather than code.

nodes.name: admin.css
nodes.summary: Complete dark-theme stylesheet for the feedback-intake admin dashboard, styling the sticky header, operations panel, filter form, feedback cards, editors, receipt tables and the screenshot viewer dialog. Imported as a text string by admin.ts and served at /admin.css.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses color-scheme: dark on :root plus a fixed 1180px body min-width, so the dashboard is deliberately desktop-only. Styles a native <dialog> screenshot viewer via the ::backdrop pseudo-element rather than a custom overlay.

nodes.name: admin.html
nodes.summary: HTML template for the feedback triage dashboard, providing the operations status panel, an add-feedback form, the search/filter form, bulk action buttons and an empty results region hydrated by the client script. Served by admin.ts with {{ADMIN_USER}} substituted at request time.
nodes.languageNotes: A server-side {{ADMIN_USER}} placeholder is the only dynamic part; everything else is hydrated client-side. Live regions (aria-live="polite") and aria-labelledby keep the async-updated panels accessible.

nodes.name: audit.html
nodes.summary: Minimal HTML template for the admin action receipts page, offering a back link, a refresh button and an empty audit container that the client script fills in. Served by admin.ts at /admin/audit.

nodes.name: configure-cloudflare-access.sh
nodes.summary: Operator script that creates or updates the path-scoped Cloudflare Access application protecting the admin dashboard, then stores the resulting team domain, JWT audience, single administrator email, and notification addresses as encrypted Worker secrets.
nodes.languageNotes: Parses .env manually rather than sourcing it (rejecting non NAME=VALUE lines and invalid identifiers), validates account id/hostname/email shapes before any API call, and is idempotent: it looks up an existing app by name and PUTs, refusing to proceed if duplicates exist.

nodes.name: api_request
nodes.summary: Wraps curl for Cloudflare API v4 calls, assembling method, path, and optional JSON body while passing the bearer token through stdin headers rather than the command line.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `--header @-` with a here-string so the API token never appears in the process argument list visible to other users.

nodes.name: require_success
nodes.summary: Asserts that a Cloudflare API response reported success, printing each returned error message and aborting the setup run otherwise.

nodes.name: put_worker_secret
nodes.summary: Pipes a secret value into `wrangler secret put` from inside the service directory so Access and notification settings land as encrypted Worker secrets.

nodes.name: migrate-feedback-database.sh
nodes.summary: Applies pending D1 migrations for the feedback service against either Wrangler's local development database (default) or the hosted Cloudflare database, with an option to fall back to Wrangler OAuth login instead of an API token.
nodes.languageNotes: Clearing CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN for the single command invocation is how `--wrangler-login` forces the interactive OAuth path without mutating the operator's environment.

nodes.name: setup-dashboard-daemon.sh
nodes.summary: One-time installer for the self-hosted dashboard: generates the .env credentials file if absent, builds the compose image, then writes and enables a root-owned systemd unit that runs the container from a protected /etc runtime directory.
nodes.languageNotes: Because the unit runs as root it refuses to reference a docker binary whose resolved path or any parent directory is group/world-writable, and it copies compose.yaml and .env into /etc so the running service does not depend on a user-writable checkout.

nodes.name: is_root_owned
nodes.summary: Reports whether a path is owned by uid 0 and carries no group- or world-write permission bits.

nodes.name: trusted_binary_path
nodes.summary: Resolves an executable candidate through symlinks and accepts it only if the binary and every ancestor directory up to / are root-owned and not writable by others, printing the trusted absolute path.
nodes.languageNotes: Walking the full ancestor chain closes the substitution hole where a writable intermediate directory would let an unprivileged user swap the binary the root systemd unit executes.

nodes.name: require_unit_safe
nodes.summary: Rejects empty values or values containing characters outside a conservative allowlist before they are interpolated into the generated systemd unit file.

nodes.name: update-dashboard-daemon.sh
nodes.summary: Refreshes an already-installed dashboard daemon: optionally fast-forwards the checkout, rebuilds the compose image with `--pull`, re-installs compose.yaml and .env into the /etc runtime directory, and restarts the systemd service.
nodes.languageNotes: Warns when the installed unit still points at the checkout instead of /etc/practice-takes-feedback, which is the migration signal to re-run the setup script.

nodes.name: .clang-format
nodes.summary: Deliberately conservative clang-format style for the C++ sources: LLVM base, 4-space indent, 100-column limit, Allman braces and no short one-line blocks, chosen so it behaves identically across the clang-format versions shipped on Windows, Linux and macOS.

nodes.name: .clang-tidy
nodes.summary: Static-analysis rule set for application-owned C++ (header filter scoped to `src/`), enabling the analyzer, bugprone, performance, portability and a curated readability subset while opting out of families that misfire on JUCE APIs; analyzer/bugprone/performance findings are warnings-as-errors.
nodes.languageNotes: `WarningsAsErrors` is a strict subset of `Checks`, so readability findings stay advisory while defect-class findings fail the gate.

nodes.name: .gitattributes
nodes.summary: Declares per-path merge behaviour for files where a line-by-line three-way merge is wrong: named drivers `merge=cmake-sources` for CMakeLists.txt and `merge=npm-lock` for the services lockfile, `merge=ours -diff` for regenerated knowledge-graph artifacts, binary treatment for SOPS ciphertext and `merge=union` for append-only manual-verification evidence.
nodes.languageNotes: Git refuses to read merge-driver definitions from a repository, so the drivers named here must be installed per clone by tools/scripts/git/configure_merge.py; without it the entries degrade to ordinary merges.

nodes.name: CODEOWNERS
nodes.summary: Single-line GitHub code-ownership rule assigning every path in the repository to the sole maintainer (@dwerkjem), matching the project's single-developer review process.

nodes.name: .sops.yaml.example
nodes.summary: Template SOPS configuration showing the single creation rule that encrypts `.secrets/**.sops` to an age recipient; it is copied to a real `.sops.yaml` by the secrets manager's `init` subcommand with the maintainer's public key substituted in.
nodes.languageNotes: Only the age public recipient is ever committed; the matching AGE-SECRET-KEY is explicitly kept out of the repository.

nodes.name: v1.schema.json
nodes.summary: JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) documenting the v1 feedback wire protocol shared by the C++ in-app feedback client and the feedback-intake Worker, defining the common `client` envelope plus the authorization and feedback request/response shapes with strict length, pattern and `unevaluatedProperties` constraints.
nodes.languageNotes: Nothing currently validates either implementation against this contract at build time, so client and server can drift from the schema.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Index for the developer documentation tree, describing what lives in each subdirectory (`build/`, `architecture/`, `quality/`, `performance/`, `operations/`, `agents/`) and listing the project's main technologies.

nodes.name: AGENT_GUIDE.md
nodes.summary: Operating guide for AI coding agents working in this repository: build/test/lint commands for the C++ app, the TypeScript worker and the Python tooling, plus the hard constraints on repository-root contents, source layering, ownership, the audio-thread boundary, test layout and versioning.

nodes.name: ARCHITECTURE.md
nodes.summary: Authoritative architecture reference covering source organization, the application ownership chain from PracticeTakesApplication down to per-tool components, the tool workspace and presentation containers, theme contrast/propagation, the audio-thread boundary, and the tuner and spectrogram analysis pipelines.

nodes.name: ARCHITECTURE_QA.md
nodes.summary: Reviewer checklist form of the architecture rules — source layering, ownership and lifetime, the audio-thread boundary, coupling and testability, scope consistency — plus guidance on when a change needs an OpenSpec proposal rather than a checklist pass.

nodes.name: audio-thread-safety.md
nodes.summary: Safety review of the performance event-capture path, documenting what the real-time audio callback is allowed to do, the lifecycle constraints on consumers draining the sample FIFO, and how the bounded-callback claim is verified.

nodes.name: hardware-acceptance.md
nodes.summary: Protocol for the hardware performance pilot: the reference machine matrix, controlled measurement conditions, representative workload, trial ordering and counts, instrumentation calibration, correctness/equivalence checks and the end-to-end acceptance and gate-approval criteria.

nodes.name: settings-defaults.md
nodes.summary: Reference for the application's persisted settings: workspace state, portable `.ptsettings` transfer, global and tuner defaults, the shipped voice and general-instrument presets, and what each reset scope clears.

nodes.name: musicxml-import/spec.md
nodes.summary: Proposed spec delta for MusicXML import, requiring support for uncompressed and compressed (.mxl) documents, a documented and enforced notation subset, conversion of supported notation into the normalized score model, and defined behaviour for out-of-order voices, pickup measures and unusable manifests.

nodes.name: normalized-score-model/spec.md
nodes.summary: Proposed spec delta for a renderer-independent score model built from parts, measures, voices and events, requiring pitches to retain both spelling and sounding number and all parts to share one musical time base regardless of their source resolution.

nodes.name: hardware-performance-lab/spec.md
nodes.summary: Proposed spec delta for the hardware Performance Lab: configuring and validating benchmark runs, executing repeated cancellable end-to-end scenarios, comparing optimization strategies fairly (rejecting incompatible comparisons), and capturing hardware/run provenance alongside user-visible and real-time measurements.

nodes.name: config.yaml
nodes.summary: OpenSpec workflow configuration selecting the `spec-driven` schema; the optional project-context and per-artifact rule sections are left as commented examples.

nodes.name: benchmark-ci-reporting/spec.md
nodes.summary: Active spec requiring the HarmonicAnalyzer, AudioSampleFifo and startup-timing benchmarks to run on pushes to main, be rendered as a readable workflow step summary, and have their raw XML uploaded as a build artifact for cross-commit comparison.

nodes.name: codeql-security-scanning/spec.md
nodes.summary: Active spec requiring CodeQL analysis to run on pull requests, on pushes to main and on a weekly schedule, covering the languages actually present in the repository.

nodes.name: cpp-pr-quality-gate/spec.md
nodes.summary: Active spec for the C++ pull-request quality gate: PRs are checked for clang-format compliance and clang-tidy findings using the same recursive file discovery as the post-merge job, and a zero-file run must fail rather than silently pass.

nodes.name: end-to-end-smoke-tests/spec.md
nodes.summary: Active spec for headless smoke testing: the built application must launch with no display and no capture device, verify startup, opening a tool and clean shutdown, distinguish crashes from hangs, and stay separable from the unit-test suite.

nodes.name: knowledge-graph-site/spec.md
nodes.summary: Active spec for publishing the repository knowledge graph as a static browsable site: it must work from a plain file server and from a subpath, build only from committed graph artifacts (failing loudly when absent), and deploy when the graph changes or on demand rather than on every source commit.

nodes.name: load-and-soak-tests/spec.md
nodes.summary: Active spec for opt-in load and soak testing of the audio sample FIFO under concurrent producers/consumers, saturation and stalled-consumer conditions, requiring sustained runs to stay bounded, the duration to be configurable, and results to be reported rather than merely passed.

nodes.name: manual-gui-verification/spec.md
nodes.summary: Active spec for the interactive manual GUI verification harness: it drives the tester through every surface automatically, scores each on three fixed axes plus optional surface-specific questions, accepts free-text notes, and records unreachable surfaces so runs stay comparable over time.

nodes.name: python-script-test-gate/spec.md
nodes.summary: Active spec for the Python tooling test gate: tests run in CI whenever Python under `tools/scripts/` changes, discovery must reach the whole scripts tree including new subdirectories, and release version bump arithmetic and malformed-version handling must be covered.

nodes.name: settings-transfer/spec.md
nodes.summary: OpenSpec capability specification for portable settings import/export: a versioned allowlist-only bundle, privacy exclusions, validate-before-apply, informed confirmation, transactional apply-or-restore, and safe fallback for machine-specific audio-device and window-bounds data.

nodes.summary: Computes the next version for a major, minor, or patch bump, resetting the lower components and rejecting unknown bump types.

nodes.name: build_parser
nodes.summary: Constructs the argparse interface exposing the current-version read and the bump subcommands.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point that reads the current version or applies a bump and reports the resulting value for the release workflow to consume.

nodes.name: setup.sh
nodes.summary: Thin launcher that puts the roadmap script directory on PYTHONPATH and execs the practice_takes_roadmap module with the caller's arguments.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses strict bash mode (set -euo pipefail) and resolves its own directory via BASH_SOURCE so it works from any working directory.

nodes.name: run_tests.py
nodes.summary: Runs every test_*.py under tools/scripts/ by loading each file by path, because unittest discovery finds nothing in these non-package directories and would leave CI green while running no tests. An empty result is a hard error.
nodes.languageNotes: Loads modules via importlib.util.spec_from_file_location under a unique name prefix, avoiding the shadowing of the standard library's secrets module by tools/scripts/secrets.

nodes.name: load_test_module
nodes.summary: Imports one test file under a unique synthetic module name derived from its path so sibling directories cannot collide or shadow stdlib modules.

nodes.name: build_suite
nodes.summary: Globs every test_*.py under the scripts root, loads each one, and aggregates them into a unittest suite, exiting with an error when no test files were found.

nodes.name: secrets_manager.py
nodes.summary: Manages developer secret files as SOPS-encrypted Git mirrors: plaintext matched by tools/secret-patterns stays local while an encrypted copy lives at .secrets/<path>.sops. Provides audit, encrypt, decrypt, sync, conflict resolve, and init commands plus a staged-plaintext guard.
nodes.languageNotes: Standard-library-only Python driving sops and git as subprocesses; writes state atomically with restrictive permissions and keeps scratch plaintext inside the .git directory.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Shared subprocess wrapper that runs a command with optional stdin and converts failures into SecretsError with the captured stderr.

nodes.name: read_patterns
nodes.summary: Parses tools/secret-patterns into ordered include/exclude rules, rejecting patterns with whitespace or parent traversal.

nodes.name: pattern_matches
nodes.summary: Matches a repository-relative path against one glob rule, giving ** the expected behaviour at both root and nested depths.

nodes.name: is_secret_path
nodes.summary: Applies the ordered rules top to bottom so a later exclusion wins, deciding whether a path is managed plaintext.

nodes.name: discover_plaintext
nodes.summary: Walks the working tree, pruning build and dependency directories, and returns every plaintext file the pattern rules select.

nodes.name: discover_mirrors
nodes.summary: Enumerates the encrypted .sops mirrors currently stored under the .secrets directory.

nodes.name: load_state
nodes.summary: Reads the per-clone sync state JSON from the Git directory, returning an empty state when it is missing or corrupt.

nodes.name: atomic_write
nodes.summary: Writes bytes through a temporary file and an atomic rename, optionally applying owner-only permissions for secret content.

nodes.name: require_sops
nodes.summary: Verifies that the sops binary and the repository's encryption configuration are present before any crypto operation is attempted.

nodes.name: encrypt_bytes
nodes.summary: Encrypts plaintext bytes into the SOPS mirror format for a given mirror path.

nodes.name: decrypt_bytes
nodes.summary: Decrypts a SOPS mirror back to plaintext bytes, surfacing sops failures as SecretsError.

nodes.name: sync_git_exclude
nodes.summary: Rewrites a managed block in .git/info/exclude so every plaintext secret pattern is ignored locally without touching the tracked .gitignore.

nodes.name: staged_plaintext_paths
nodes.summary: Lists staged files that the pattern rules classify as plaintext secrets.

nodes.name: protect_staged_plaintext
nodes.summary: Guard that unstages any plaintext secret about to be committed, keeping the encrypted mirror as the only committed representation.

nodes.name: audit_command
nodes.summary: Reports which plaintext secrets exist, which mirrors are present, and whether any plaintext is tracked by Git.

nodes.name: encrypt_command
nodes.summary: Encrypts every discovered plaintext secret into its mirror, records hashes in state, and optionally protects the index in the same pass.

nodes.name: decrypt_command
nodes.summary: Restores plaintext files from their encrypted mirrors, refusing to overwrite locally modified plaintext unless forced.

nodes.name: sync_command
nodes.summary: Reconciles plaintext and mirrors in both directions using recorded hashes, applying the caller's preference and recording a conflict copy when both sides changed.

nodes.name: merge_plaintext
nodes.summary: Three-way merges decrypted plaintext versions via git merge-file, producing clean output for disjoint edits and conflict markers otherwise.

nodes.name: resolve_command
nodes.summary: Drives resolution of unmerged encrypted mirrors: decrypts the ours/base/theirs stages into scratch space inside .git, merges or takes a chosen side, then re-encrypts and finishes the resolution.

nodes.name: init_command
nodes.summary: Bootstraps a clone: writes the default pattern file and a SOPS configuration whose creation rule regex matches mirror paths for the supplied age recipient.

nodes.name: build_parser
nodes.summary: Defines the argparse surface for the init, audit, encrypt, decrypt, sync, resolve, and index-protection subcommands.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point that resolves the repository root, dispatches the chosen subcommand, and turns SecretsError into a readable non-zero exit.

nodes.name: test_secrets_manager.py
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the SOPS secrets manager, covering glob rule ordering, mirror path round-tripping, path-traversal rejection, real repository pattern selection, conflict cleanup, and three-way plaintext merges.

nodes.name: PatternTests
nodes.summary: Covers glob semantics for ** at root and nested depth, ordered exclusions winning, mirror path round-tripping, and rejection of traversal or whitespace patterns.

nodes.name: RepositoryPatternTests
nodes.summary: Runs the real tools/secret-patterns rules to assert managed plaintext is selected while templates and source files are not.

nodes.name: InitTests
nodes.summary: Asserts that init writes a SOPS creation-rule regex that actually matches generated mirror paths.

nodes.name: SyncConflictTests
nodes.summary: Checks that conflict copies written during sync are removed once the conflict is resolved.

nodes.name: PlaintextMergeTests
nodes.summary: Verifies three-way merge behaviour for disjoint and overlapping secret edits and that scratch plaintext never leaves the .git directory.

nodes.name: secret-patterns
nodes.summary: Ordered glob rule list naming the plaintext secret files that must stay local and be mirrored encrypted, with ! exclusions keeping example and template files committable as plaintext.
nodes.languageNotes: Rules are evaluated top to bottom so a later ! exclusion overrides an earlier match — the same ordering convention as .gitignore but with explicit precedence.

nodes.name: vcpkg.json
nodes.summary: vcpkg manifest pinning a builtin baseline and the native dependencies (ALSA, curl with SSL only, fontconfig, freetype, JACK, and the X11 libraries) needed to build the JUCE application. Its version-string is written by the release version manager.
nodes.languageNotes: builtin-baseline pins the whole dependency set to one vcpkg commit, making native builds reproducible across machines.

tour.title: What Practice Takes Is
tour.description: Start with the README to learn what this project actually does: a desktop music-practice application built on JUCE 8 and C++20 that currently ships a tuner, a spectrogram, and a harmonic analyzer inside a dockable workspace. It also introduces the two things that shape almost every design decision downstream — a single shared microphone capture path feeding several tools at once, and portable `.ptsettings` import/export. Keep the tool list in mind: nearly every later step is either that capture path, one of those tools, or the shell that hosts them.

tour.title: How the App Is Built
tour.description: The root CMake file is the project's real table of contents: it pins JUCE 8.0.12 and Catch2 v3.8.1, declares the `PracticeTakes` GUI application with its full source list, gates optional features like the Performance Lab and coverage behind configure-time options, and builds the `PracticeTakesTests` target. Its first job, though, is reading and validating `tools/VERSION`, a single `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` line that is the sole source of truth for the app version and is propagated from here into JUCE metadata and the window title. Nothing else in the tree hardcodes a version — if you need it, you read it from CMake's propagation, not a copy.
tour.languageLesson: CMake `FetchContent` pins dependencies by tag so the build is reproducible without vendoring source. Option variables (`option(...)`) let one CMakeLists describe several build shapes — debug app, test binary, instrumented Performance Lab — instead of maintaining separate build files.

tour.title: Entry Point and the Shell
tour.description: `main.cpp` is the JUCE application entry: it defines the application object, creates the top-level `DocumentWindow`, and hands the interior over to a single `MainComponent`. That `MainComponent` is the shell, and its header is the highest fan-in file in the whole codebase — it owns the one shared `AudioDeviceManager`, the application look-and-feel, the settings and feedback windows, and one live component per open tool along with that tool's presentation container. Its implementation is deliberately split across several `MainComponent*.cpp` files by responsibility, so treat this header as the map of what the shell is responsible for rather than expecting one giant source file.
tour.languageLesson: The ownership convention here is RAII: single-owner objects are held by `std::unique_ptr` and shared long-lived services are passed as references, never as raw owning pointers. Reading a JUCE class header top-to-bottom tells you the ownership graph, because members are the ownership.

tour.title: The Real-Time Audio Boundary
tour.description: This is the project's one hard constraint, and understanding it explains the shape of everything above it. `AudioInputService::audioDeviceIOCallbackWithContext` runs on the real-time audio thread, so it must stay strictly bounded — no heap allocation, no locks, no file or network I/O, no logging, no UI updates, and absolutely no FFT or pitch detection. All it does is clear output, read atomic mute/gain values, measure peak, and copy samples into one preallocated 65,536-sample single-producer/single-consumer `AudioSampleFifo` per active tool. Each tool then drains its own FIFO from a message-thread timer, which is why a slow tool can never stall capture or starve another tool; `AudioRecoveryPolicy` is the JUCE-free rule deciding when a lost device warrants a reconnect attempt.
tour.languageLesson: An SPSC (single-producer/single-consumer) ring buffer lets two threads exchange data with only atomic index updates and no mutex — safe precisely because exactly one thread writes and one reads. Device state changes cross the boundary the same way: written as `std::atomic` flags and polled from a timer, never as shared mutable state guarded by a lock the audio thread would have to wait on.

tour.title: A Tool on That Foundation: The Tuner
tour.description: The tuner is the clearest example of a consumer built on the FIFO contract from Step 4. `PitchDetector` implements FFT-accelerated normalized autocorrelation with RMS gating, a 16.35 Hz–2500 Hz search range, a minimum correlation score to reject noise, and parabolic interpolation to refine the peak to sub-bin accuracy. Critically, all of that runs on the message thread, driven by the tuner's own timer draining its own FIFO — never in the audio callback. `TunerComponent` is the thin JUCE layer that pulls samples, calls the detector, and renders the result.

tour.title: Spectrogram and Harmonics
tour.description: The other two analysis tools follow the identical pattern, which is what makes the pattern worth learning once. The spectrogram drains its own FIFO and renders a scrolling time-frequency image; the harmonic analyzer reuses `PitchDetector` from Step 5 to find the fundamental, then takes a Hann-windowed magnitude spectrum, samples the first eight partials, and derives spectral centroid, confidence, and inharmonicity. Note the boundary rule this illustrates: a tool under `src/features/*` may reuse shared infrastructure, but must never reach into another tool's internals — anything genuinely shared belongs in `src/platform` or `src/application`.

tour.title: The Testability Split
tour.description: This project deliberately extracts pure logic — state machines, layout trees, policy decisions — out of JUCE `Component` classes so it can be unit tested with no display attached. `WorkspaceLayoutState` is the exemplar: it has no JUCE dependency at all and is fully covered by a Catch2 suite, exactly as `AudioRecoveryPolicy` was in Step 4. `TEST_LAYOUT.md` explains the convention that makes this navigable — `src/tests/` mirrors the structure of `src/`, so the tests for any file live at the parallel path. When you add non-trivial logic, follow this split rather than burying it in a `Component` subclass.
tour.languageLesson: Header-only pure logic in C++ is easy to test because it links into a test binary with no framework runtime. Catch2 v3 lets you tag test cases (`[tag]`) and select them from the CLI, so `build/bin/PracticeTakesTests "[workspace]"` runs one subsystem's suite in isolation.

tour.title: The Workspace Presentation System
tour.description: Building on the layout state from Step 7, these three containers are how a tool is actually shown: docked in a titled panel, floating in its own window, or grouped into tabs. The key design decision is stated in each of them — a presentation container hosts but never owns the tool component. Because `MainComponent` (Step 3) holds the sole ownership, moving a tool between docked, floating, and tabbed presentation merely reparents the component, preserving its analysis state and its registration with the shared audio service instead of destroying and rebuilding it.

tour.title: Settings and the Portable Codec
tour.description: Settings persistence writes the user's configuration — including the workspace layout from Step 8 — so a session can be restored on next launch. The transfer codec is the more interesting half: it encodes settings into a versioned JSON document for the portable `.ptsettings` format, and decodes it back under explicit size and nesting-depth budgets. Rather than silently accepting whatever a hostile or corrupt file contains, a partially valid document decodes to a `recovered` status with the salvageable fields applied, so the failure mode is visible instead of silent.
tour.languageLesson: Explicit budgets (max document size, max nesting depth, max element counts) are the standard defence for any parser reading untrusted input — without them a small file can expand into unbounded work or stack depth. Versioning the document format up front means old files stay readable as the schema evolves.

tour.title: The Score Model
tour.description: The score model is groundwork rather than shipped UI, and it is worth reading as a statement of intent. `Score` is a normalized, engraving-independent tree — metadata, tick base, parts with their measures and declared divisions, a tempo map, and importer diagnostics — designed to be shared across threads as `shared_ptr<const Score>`. `MusicalTime` and `TempoMap` supply the time domain: musical positions in ticks and the mapping from those to wall-clock seconds. Like the policy headers in Steps 4 and 7, this layer is entirely JUCE-free, which is what will let notation rendering and MIDI/MusicXML import be built and tested against it independently.
tour.languageLesson: Sharing immutable data as `std::shared_ptr<const T>` gives lock-free multi-threaded reads: readers can never mutate, and an update publishes a whole new object rather than editing one in place. This is the same principle as the audio boundary in Step 4 — avoid shared mutable state instead of guarding it.

tour.title: Feedback, End to End
tour.description: This is the one path in the repository that crosses from C++ into a deployed service, so it shows how the two halves of the project agree on anything. The in-app `FeedbackComponent` collects a submission and posts it; the JSON Schema documents the v1 wire protocol — a shared `client` envelope plus authorization and feedback request/response shapes with strict length, pattern, and `unevaluatedProperties` constraints; and the Cloudflare Worker's `index.ts` is the receiving end. Note the honest gap: the schema documents the contract, but nothing currently validates either side against it, so client and worker can drift.
tour.languageLesson: JSON Schema's `unevaluatedProperties: false` rejects any field not accounted for by the schema and its composed subschemas — stricter than `additionalProperties`, which does not see through `allOf`. A schema is only a contract if something executes it; otherwise it is documentation that ages.

tour.title: The Performance Lab
tour.description: The Performance Lab is opt-in instrumentation, compiled in only when configured with `-DPRACTICE_TAKES_ENABLE_PERFORMANCE_LAB=ON`. Its architecture is the clearest dependency-inversion example in the tree: `BenchmarkInterfaces` declares the abstract collaborators, and `BenchmarkRunner` receives its stabilizer, progress observer, aggregator, and cancellation predicate as injected `std::function` callbacks rather than constructing them. That means the runner's phase logic can be exercised in unit tests with fakes, no timing hardware or real workload required — the Step 7 testability split applied to a whole subsystem.
tour.languageLesson: `std::function` as an injection point is C++'s lightweight alternative to an abstract base class: the caller passes any lambda or callable matching the signature, so tests substitute behaviour without a class hierarchy. The cost is a possible heap allocation and an indirect call — acceptable off the audio thread, but never inside the Step 4 callback.

tour.title: How Quality Is Enforced
tour.description: The CI workflows encode the rules the earlier steps described. The C++ quality workflow runs `clang-format` and `clang-tidy` (check-only on PRs, auto-fixing on `main`), while the coverage workflow builds the Catch2 suite and reports on it. Two Python gates back the conventions directly: `check_test_layout.py` enforces the `src/tests/` mirroring rule from Step 7, and `check_manual_verification.py` refuses to build release artifacts unless a complete manual GUI verification run covers the commit being released — decided by commit ancestry plus a diff against release-affecting paths, with `src/tests/` exempt.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions workflows key off `on` triggers, run `jobs` in parallel, and execute `steps` sequentially within a job. Splitting checks into separate workflows (quality, coverage) means one failing gate does not mask the others' results, and each can cache its own toolchain.

tour.title: Conventions Worth Knowing
tour.description: Two documents close the loop on how to work in this repository. The agent guide is the substantive contributor and assistant handbook — the root `CLAUDE.md` is a stub that points here — covering when a change goes straight to a PR versus when it needs an OpenSpec proposal under `openspec/changes/`. The merging document explains the repository's opt-in custom Git merge drivers (`cmake-sources`, `npm-lock`, `ours` for generated `.ua/` files, `union` for manual-run records), why Git deliberately forbids defining drivers inside a clone, and how to bypass or remove them. Read both before your first change: they prevent the two most common surprises, proposing too little process and hitting an unexplained merge result.
